Title: MACHINE LEARNING APPLICATIONS IN OPTIC NERVE HEAD AND LAMINA CRIBROSA BIOMECHANICS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
Snippet: By combining the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from three related research, this meta-analysis summarizes the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-based models for glaucoma detection. The analysis attempts to establish a core and more reliable measure of diagnostic accuracy that represents general model performance rather than study-specific results by combining evidence from several investigations. In order to improve the generalizability of the pooled estimate and enable meaningful comparison across various AI frameworks, the chosen studies make use of a variety of datasets, methodological approaches, and validation strategies. The meta-analysis not only determines a summary AUC but also methodically assesses study heterogeneity and looks for potential bias resulting from sample selection, model training methods, or reporting standards. 

Determining the dependability and clinical usability of AI-driven glaucoma screening systems requires evaluating publication bias and methodological heterogeneity. All things considered, this combined research presents a comprehensive evaluation of the state of AI in glaucoma detection and sheds light on the coherence, advantages, and disadvantages of the available data. The AUC values from the five studies that reported this metric-Thiéry, Pourjavan, Mehta, Chuangsuwanich (strain + PointNet), and Braeu-were combined for the formal meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy. Comparable quantitative results appropriate for aggregation were obtained from these investigations. The remaining studies provide important qualitative information about the risk of glaucoma progression, biomechanical mechanisms, and morphometric features; however, they were not able to be included in the numerical pooling for the AUC-based meta-analysis because they did not report AUCs or similar diagnostic metrics. An overall AUC of around 0.95 (95% CI: 0.94-0.96) was obtained from the pooled analysis, demonstrating the high diagnostic accuracy of AI models for glaucoma detection across several modalities. With Thiéry, Pourjavan, and Mehta reporting high performance values above 0.95, the forest plot shows a comparatively tight grouping of study-specific AUCs.

Title: A systematic review, meta-analysis, and network analysis of diagnostic microRNAs in glaucoma
Snippet: The meta-analysis included studies that detected a single dysregulated microRNA in glaucoma cases compared to controls and the corresponding AUC, sensitivity, and specificity for the discovered microRNA. Using these criteria, four studies identified 12 individual microRNAs. The associated forest plot depicts the sensitivity (95% CIs) and specificity (95% CIs) for each microRNA (Fig. 4). Overall sensitivity and specificity of the 12 individual microRNAs in the diagnosis of glaucoma were 80% [95% CI 73-86%, test of heterogeneity: Q = 15.29, I 2 = 28.08%, p-value = 0.17] and 74% [95% CI 63-83%, test of heterogeneity: Q = 28.15, I 2 = 60.9%, p-value = 0.00], respectively. These findings suggest that utilizing microRNAs as biomarkers has a high discriminative ability in detecting glaucoma. For glaucoma detection, the slope coefficient was related to a p-value of 0.83 (Fig. 5), indicating no publication bias in our meta-analysis. In addition, the pooled diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) of the 12 individual microRNAs in the diagnosis of glaucoma was 11.2 [95% CI 5.3-24]. Afterward, random-effects models were used to re-analyze the data, and the diagnostic threshold was investigated. The Spearman's correlation coefficient was − 0.130 (p-value = 0.687), indicating that the diagnostic threshold was not responsible for the heterogeneity. Disparities in study techniques, specimen type, endogenous reference, or total sample size may also contribute to the existing heterogeneity. The publication bias  of meta-analysis in diagnostic accuracy was investigated using Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test, depicted in Fig. 6. The most well-known reporting bias is publication bias. It is the outcome of relevant trials being published or not, depending on the type and direction of the results. A paper, for instance, is more likely to be published if the findings are significant.

Title: Dry Eye Disease and Tear Cytokine Levels—A Meta-Analysis
Snippet: Two reviewers (MR, LT) independently extracted the following data from each included publication: first author name; year of publication; location; cytokine(s) measured; the assay technology; scales that were employed for cytokine measurement; tear sample collection; DED etiology; numbers of subjects; demographic characteristics (e.g., age and sex); tear cytokine levels (mean and standard deviation [SD]) in both the patient and the control groups. Studies with data reported in figures or with missing data were excluded in the quantitative synthesis. In case of discrepancies between the two reviewers, the manuscripts were revisited and agreed on by discussion.

In our meta-analysis, no signs of heterogeneity were observed for sensitivity results (I 2 = 0%), but substantial heterogeneity was observed for specificity (I 2 = 73.4%). 

To find the source of heterogeneity, we performed a subgroup analysis based on the mfVEP registry team (Veris and Accumap), assay methods (ASI and Cluster) and glaucoma severity depending on SAP mean deviation (MD). However, heterogeneity for specificity remained high, with an inconsistency rate (I 2 ) greater than 50%, while heterogeneity for sensitivity in all subgroups was I 2 = 0%. Our review includes just 241 glaucoma patients and six articles in the meta-analysis, and we are aware that when a meta-analysis includes fewer than 500 patients and fewer than 15 trials, there may be fluctuations in I 2 estimates [49]. 

After excluding articles one by one through sensitivity analysis, the inconsistency rate for sensitivity heterogeneity was found to be 0%. However, the inconsistency rate for specificity was greater than 50%. Sensitivity, specificity, area under the curve (AUC) and 95% confidence interval (CI) were similar and overlapped with each other. The heterogeneity remained the same. Sensitivity analysis showed that the pooled estimates were stable and reliable. 

A Spearman rank correlation was performed, which provided a value of −0.464 (p = 0.354); in addition to the sROC, a "shoulder-arm" pattern was not appreciated, which means that there was no threshold effect between the included studies. 

We calculated the AUC of the sROC to evaluate the overall performance of the mfVEP amplitude for the diagnosis of visual field defects in glaucoma (Figure 4) and the value was 0.97. Due to the heterogeneity that existed in specificity, we did the statistical summary using the random effects model. 

A funnel plot was also constructed to assess publication bias in the meta-analysis. The data points had a symmetric funnel shape, meaning the absence of publication bias.

documents.title: MACHINE LEARNING APPLICATIONS IN OPTIC NERVE HEAD AND LAMINA CRIBROSA BIOMECHANICS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
documents.snippet:
By combining the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from three related research, this meta-analysis summarizes the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-based models for glaucoma detection. The analysis attempts to establish a core and more reliable measure of diagnostic accuracy that represents general model performance rather than study-specific results by combining evidence from several investigations. In order to improve the generalizability of the pooled estimate and enable meaningful comparison across various AI frameworks, the chosen studies make use of a variety of datasets, methodological approaches, and validation strategies. The meta-analysis not only determines a summary AUC but also methodically assesses study heterogeneity and looks for potential bias resulting from sample selection, model training methods, or reporting standards. 

Determining the dependability and clinical usability of AI-driven glaucoma screening systems requires evaluating publication bias and methodological heterogeneity. All things considered, this combined research presents a comprehensive evaluation of the state of AI in glaucoma detection and sheds light on the coherence, advantages, and disadvantages of the available data. The AUC values from the five studies that reported this metric-Thiéry, Pourjavan, Mehta, Chuangsuwanich (strain + PointNet), and Braeu-were combined for the formal meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy. Comparable quantitative results appropriate for aggregation were obtained from these investigations. The remaining studies provide important qualitative information about the risk of glaucoma progression, biomechanical mechanisms, and morphometric features; however, they were not able to be included in the numerical pooling for the AUC-based meta-analysis because they did not report AUCs or similar diagnostic metrics. An overall AUC of around 0.95 (95% CI: 0.94-0.96) was obtained from the pooled analysis, demonstrating the high diagnostic accuracy of AI models for glaucoma detection across several modalities. With Thiéry, Pourjavan, and Mehta reporting high performance values above 0.95, the forest plot shows a comparatively tight grouping of study-specific AUCs.

documents.title: A systematic review, meta-analysis, and network analysis of diagnostic microRNAs in glaucoma
documents.snippet: The meta-analysis included studies that detected a single dysregulated microRNA in glaucoma cases compared to controls and the corresponding AUC, sensitivity, and specificity for the discovered microRNA. Using these criteria, four studies identified 12 individual microRNAs. The associated forest plot depicts the sensitivity (95% CIs) and specificity (95% CIs) for each microRNA (Fig. 4). Overall sensitivity and specificity of the 12 individual microRNAs in the diagnosis of glaucoma were 80% [95% CI 73-86%, test of heterogeneity: Q = 15.29, I 2 = 28.08%, p-value = 0.17] and 74% [95% CI 63-83%, test of heterogeneity: Q = 28.15, I 2 = 60.9%, p-value = 0.00], respectively. These findings suggest that utilizing microRNAs as biomarkers has a high discriminative ability in detecting glaucoma. For glaucoma detection, the slope coefficient was related to a p-value of 0.83 (Fig. 5), indicating no publication bias in our meta-analysis. In addition, the pooled diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) of the 12 individual microRNAs in the diagnosis of glaucoma was 11.2 [95% CI 5.3-24]. Afterward, random-effects models were used to re-analyze the data, and the diagnostic threshold was investigated. The Spearman's correlation coefficient was − 0.130 (p-value = 0.687), indicating that the diagnostic threshold was not responsible for the heterogeneity. Disparities in study techniques, specimen type, endogenous reference, or total sample size may also contribute to the existing heterogeneity. The publication bias  of meta-analysis in diagnostic accuracy was investigated using Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test, depicted in Fig. 6. The most well-known reporting bias is publication bias. It is the outcome of relevant trials being published or not, depending on the type and direction of the results. A paper, for instance, is more likely to be published if the findings are significant.

Summary
- Bottom line: There is no clear evidence from 2014–2024 meta-analyses that IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α show equivalent diagnostic performance as tear biomarkers for glaucoma; instead, these cytokines should be evaluated separately due to heterogeneous tear sampling, assay methods, clinical confounders, and disease-specific context, with at least partial convergent evidence that IL‑6 is altered in glaucoma and several cytokines including IL‑1β and TNF‑α show disease-associated elevations in related ocular conditions and specific glaucoma cohorts. <cite id="43e354e3-0">Mean concentrations of multiple tear cytokines differed between early primary open-angle glaucoma and control eyes, supporting a role for tear cytokines as biomarkers</cite> <cite id="43e354e3-3">Meta-analytic evidence in dry eye shows higher IL‑1β, IL‑6, IL‑8, IL‑10, IFN‑γ, and TNF‑α in tears of dry eye disease versus controls, but emphasizes high inter-individual variability and methodological heterogeneity limiting use of fixed cutoffs</cite> <cite id="1bd32913-2">A glaucoma-focused meta-analysis subgroup found higher IL‑6 levels (SMD 0.80, 95% CI 0.26–1.35), with substantial heterogeneity by disease type, sample source, and quantification method</cite> <cite id="1f04bd07-1">In keratoprosthesis type 1, tears from eyes with glaucoma showed increases in TNF‑α and IL‑1β compared to glaucoma‑free eyes, with correlations to IOP and cup-to-disc ratio</cite> <cite id="1f04bd07-3">Comparative tear–aqueous humor analysis concluded tear cannot substitute for aqueous humor for diagnostic purposes, underscoring biologic and methodological differences</cite>.

What meta-analyses show about tear cytokines and diagnostic biomarkers
- Directionality across ocular disease: Meta-analysis in dry eye disease (DED) demonstrates consistent elevation of IL‑1β, IL‑6, IL‑8, IL‑10, IFN‑γ, and TNF‑α in tears versus controls, strengthening the concept that tear cytokines reflect inflammatory activity; however, large standard deviations and variable procedures (collection, storage, assay) limit estimation of reference intervals and cutoffs and call the biomarker utility an “unmet need.” <cite id="43e354e3-3">This meta-analysis reports significantly higher concentrations of IL‑1β, IL‑6, IL‑8, IL‑10, IFN‑γ, and TNF‑α in DED tears relative to age-matched non‑DED controls</cite> <cite id="43e354e3-3">Substantial inter-individual variation and heterogeneous sampling/assay methods preclude reliable reference ranges and cutoffs, impeding biomarker use</cite>.

Glaucoma-specific meta-analytic and pooled evidence for each cytokine
- IL‑6: A systematic review and meta-analysis covering ocular diseases reported that glaucoma (including POAG and PACG) is associated with higher intraocular IL‑6 levels (pooled SMD ≈ 0.80), with heterogeneity robust across subgroup analyses; this supports altered IL‑6 in glaucoma but does not establish diagnostic equivalence to other cytokines and underscores the need for disease- and method-specific interpretation. <cite id="1bd32913-2">Glaucoma (divided into POAG, PACG, and secondary) subgroup analyses showed higher IL‑6 levels (SMD = 0.80, 95% CI 0.26–1.35), with sensitivity analyses and meta-regression indicating robustness but substantial heterogeneity</cite>.
- IL‑1β and TNF‑α: In glaucoma cohorts with confounding by ocular surgery (keratoprosthesis), tear IL‑1β and TNF‑α were elevated in glaucoma-affected eyes and correlated with disease severity (IOP, CDR), indicating diagnostic-relevant associations in that setting; however, this evidence comes from a specialized population and single-center designs, not pooled meta-analyses across general glaucoma cohorts. <cite id="1f04bd07-1">Keratoprosthesis type 1 eyes with glaucoma had increased tear TNF‑α and IL‑1β versus glaucoma-free eyes, with positive correlations to IOP and cup-to-disc ratio</cite> <cite id="1f04bd07-2">These elevated tear cytokines (IL‑1β, TNF‑α, IFN‑γ, FGF‑basic) were specific to glaucoma-affected KPro eyes and suggested utility for future glaucoma risk stratification once validated</cite>.
- General tear cytokine differences in glaucoma: In early POAG versus controls, several tear cytokines (including IL‑6) were altered, with multiplex immunoassays detecting broad dynamic ranges and low detection limits; age and visual function were similar between groups, while structural glaucoma damage (C/D ratio) differed, supporting biological relevance of cytokine changes to glaucoma pathology. <cite id="43e354e3-0">Mean concentrations of nine tear cytokines differed between early POAG and controls, with several proinflammatory cytokines altered</cite> <cite id="43e354e3-2">Tear cytokines spanned 10–100-fold ranges; controls and POAG had similar IOP and acuity, but significant cup-to-disc differences</cite>.

Why equivalence cannot be assumed and why separate evaluation is warranted
- Heterogeneity of tear sampling and assays: Standardization gaps across tear collection (Schirmer strips, capillaries, tubes), storage, and multiplex immunoassay platforms drive inconsistent cytokine concentrations, undermining pooled equivalence testing across IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α in diagnostic terms. <cite id="43e354e3-3">Different sampling procedures change cytokine concentrations and few studies report validated SOPs, limiting reference intervals and cutoffs</cite> <cite id="1bd32913-2">Meta-regression showed disease type, quantification method, and ethnicity explain heterogeneity in IL‑6 pooled estimates</cite>.

- Evaluation should be separate but comparative: Treat IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α as distinct biomarkers with separate ROC-derived cutoffs, sensitivity/specificity, and AUCs in your population, while testing combined panels via machine learning to capture complementary information; report tear sampling and assay SOPs to enable meta-analytic synthesis in future. <cite id="43e354e3-3">Meta-analytic work emphasizes SOPs and the need for population-specific reference intervals and cutoffs due to high variability</cite>.

Snippet: Tear, as a noninvasively collectable bodily fluid, is constantly available and an important resource for follow-up studies. Different studies have examined the composition of tears and of aqueous humour in glaucoma and other eye diseases, but no previous comparative study examining the cytokine levels in tears and aqueous humour was carried out. After critical examination of the data obtained for tear and AH, we have compared the level of cytokines between these two sample types. All studied cytokines and chemokine molecules, except IL-2, showed statistically significantly higher levels in tears compared to AH (Fig. 2, Table 1). 

Based on our data, we can conclude that tear and aqueous humour are not identical from the inflammatory point of view and tear cannot substitute for aqueous humour for diagnostic purposes. Most probably, the levels of cytokines in the two sample types are controlled by different mechanisms. The higher cytokine levels in tear compared to aqueous humour might reflect not only the glaucoma-related, but also the eyedrop-or other factors-induced pro-inflammatory conditions, as well. A limitation of the study is the relatively low number of the participants recruited. Larger studies are needed to validate our findings and also to be able to do a proper patient stratification based on the drugs used.

Snippet: In addition to pointing to several new cytokine and glaucoma correlations in KPro patients, we also identified correlations between cytokine levels and IOP and CDR which were significantly positive and clinically relevant. 

In conclusion, we showed that TNF-α, IL-1β, FGF-basic and IFN-ɣ levels were elevated only in KPro eyes with glaucoma, and not in KPro eyes without glaucoma which had cytokine variations similar to those of normal eyes. These elevated cytokine levels correlated with IOP elevation and optic nerve excavation. Ocular surface inflammatory mediators may represent intraocular mechanisms of glaucoma damage. Tear fluid profile of KPro patients with glaucoma corroborates for the first time the reported elevation of TNF-α and IL-1β in preclinical models. This study provides novel insights into the mechanisms by which KPro surgery may lead to chronic inflammation and glaucoma in humans. Although cytokine levels may be variable in tear film, tear fluid is readily accessible compared to aqueous humor, and its cytokines are objectively quantifiable compared to IOP measured in KPro eyes. For these reasons, tear fluid cytokine analysis may become a useful tool in the future for glaucoma risk stratification of KPro patients, once validated in further studies. This new knowledge provides us with important and easily accessible biomarkers to follow disease progression in a more personalized fashion. Also, these data are crucial for suggesting disease pathways that may be amenable to the development of targeted therapies aimed at saving eyes from devastating consequences of glaucoma progression after KPro.

Title: Integration of tear fluid biomarkers and machine learning for the early detection of keratoconus
Snippet: This study aimed to explore the diagnostic potential of tear fluid biomarkers and clinical parameters for early KC and to evaluate the accuracy of ML models in predicting early KC. We detected elevated levels of cytokines (IL-1β, Galectin-1, and Galectin-3) in the tear fluid of patients with KC and early KC, suggesting their role as potential biomarkers for this disease. Among the nine ML models evaluated, the random forest model demonstrated superior predictive performance, particularly when trained with both tear fluid biomarkers and clinical parameters. The random forest model, retrained using Pentacam parameters (D-index, BE, and Kmax) and tear biomarkers (Galectin-1, Galectin-3, and IL-1β), the top three ranked features of the two clusters based on importance scores, demonstrated optimal performance in predicting early KC. 

Our findings align with those of previous studies that highlighted the role of tear fluid biomarkers in KC diagnosis [26]. Inflammatory cytokines in tears, such as IL-1β, which were significantly elevated in our study, have been implicated in the pathophysiology of KC, likely by contributing to keratocyte apoptosis, tissue degradation, and remodeling [7,11]. These findings corroborate earlier work that identified proinflammatory cytokines as closely associated with the progression and severity of KC [27,28]. Although IL-1β level appeared slightly higher in early KC than in KC, this difference was not statistically significant. Its consistent elevation compared with that of the controls and strong predictive contribution in the model may support its utility as an early diagnostic rather than a progression-related biomarker. 

Moreover, our study highlighted elevated levels of Galectin-1 and Galectin-3 in tear fluid, which exhibited high feature importance scores in the early KC prediction model, thus underscoring their potential as diagnostic biomarkers. Galectins are a family of lectins characterized by their specific binding affinity for β-galactosidase carbohydrates and a conserved consensus amino acid sequence within the carbohydrate recognition domain (CRD).

Summary
- Bottom line: There is no clear evidence from 2014–2024 meta-analyses that IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α show equivalent diagnostic performance as tear biomarkers for glaucoma; instead, these cytokines should be evaluated separately due to heterogeneous tear sampling, assay methods, clinical confounders, and disease-specific context, with at least partial convergent evidence that IL‑6 is altered in glaucoma and several cytokines including IL‑1β and TNF‑α show disease-associated elevations in related ocular conditions and specific glaucoma cohorts. <cite id="43e354e3-0">Mean concentrations of multiple tear cytokines differed between early primary open-angle glaucoma and control eyes, supporting a role for tear cytokines as biomarkers</cite> <cite id="43e354e3-3">Meta-analytic evidence in dry eye shows higher IL‑1β, IL‑6, IL‑8, IL‑10, IFN‑γ, and TNF‑α in tears of dry eye disease versus controls, but emphasizes high inter-individual variability and methodological heterogeneity limiting use of fixed cutoffs</cite> <cite id="1bd32913-2">A glaucoma-focused meta-analysis subgroup found higher IL‑6 levels (SMD 0.80, 95% CI 0.26–1.35), with substantial heterogeneity by disease type, sample source, and quantification method</cite> <cite id="1f04bd07-1">In keratoprosthesis type 1, tears from eyes with glaucoma showed increases in TNF‑α and IL‑1β compared to glaucoma‑free eyes, with correlations to IOP and cup-to-disc ratio</cite> <cite id="1f04bd07-3">Comparative tear–aqueous humor analysis concluded tear cannot substitute for aqueous humor for diagnostic purposes, underscoring biologic and methodological differences</cite>.

What meta-analyses show about tear cytokines and diagnostic biomarkers
- Directionality across ocular disease: Meta-analysis in dry eye disease (DED) demonstrates consistent elevation of IL‑1β, IL‑6, IL‑8, IL‑10, IFN‑γ, and TNF‑α in tears versus controls, strengthening the concept that tear cytokines reflect inflammatory activity; however, large standard deviations and variable procedures (collection, storage, assay) limit estimation of reference intervals and cutoffs and call the biomarker utility an “unmet need.” <cite id="43e354e3-3">This meta-analysis reports significantly higher concentrations of IL‑1β, IL‑6, IL‑8, IL‑10, IFN‑γ, and TNF‑α in DED tears relative to age-matched non‑DED controls</cite> <cite id="43e354e3-3">Substantial inter-individual variation and heterogeneous sampling/assay methods preclude reliable reference ranges and cutoffs, impeding biomarker use</cite>.
- Variability and confounding: Cross-study heterogeneity is large, with different sampling (Schirmer strips vs. microcapillaries, etc.) and assay platforms producing different cytokine concentrations; meta-analyses and systematic reviews highlight heterogeneity and potential publication bias, with subgroup analyses showing effects depend on ethnicity, disease type, sample source, and quantification method. <cite id="1bd32913-2">Substantial heterogeneity in IL‑6 meta-analysis led to subgroup analyses by disease (POAG, PACG, secondary glaucoma), sample type, ethnicity, quantification method, and meta-regression showed disease type, quantification method, and ethnicity significantly associated with heterogeneity</cite> <cite id="43e354e3-3">Different tear sampling procedures can alter cytokine concentrations, and few studies report validated standard operating procedures</cite>.

Glaucoma-specific meta-analytic and pooled evidence for each cytokine
- IL‑6: A systematic review and meta-analysis covering ocular diseases reported that glaucoma (including POAG and PACG) is associated with higher intraocular IL‑6 levels (pooled SMD ≈ 0.80), with heterogeneity robust across subgroup analyses; this supports altered IL‑6 in glaucoma but does not establish diagnostic equivalence to other cytokines and underscores the need for disease- and method-specific interpretation. <cite id="1bd32913-2">Glaucoma (divided into POAG, PACG, and secondary) subgroup analyses showed higher IL‑6 levels (SMD = 0.80, 95% CI 0.26–1.35), with sensitivity analyses and meta-regression indicating robustness but substantial heterogeneity</cite>.
- IL‑1β and TNF‑α: In glaucoma cohorts with confounding by ocular surgery (keratoprosthesis), tear IL‑1β and TNF‑α were elevated in glaucoma-affected eyes and correlated with disease severity (IOP, CDR), indicating diagnostic-relevant associations in that setting; however, this evidence comes from a specialized population and single-center designs, not pooled meta-analyses across general glaucoma cohorts. <cite id="1f04bd07-1">Keratoprosthesis type 1 eyes with glaucoma had increased tear TNF‑α and IL‑1β versus glaucoma-free eyes, with positive correlations to IOP and cup-to-disc ratio</cite> <cite id="1f04bd07-2">These elevated tear cytokines (IL‑1β, TNF‑α, IFN‑γ, FGF‑basic) were specific to glaucoma-affected KPro eyes and suggested utility for future glaucoma risk stratification once validated</cite>.
- General tear cytokine differences in glaucoma: In early POAG versus controls, several tear cytokines (including IL‑6) were altered, with multiplex immunoassays detecting broad dynamic ranges and low detection limits; age and visual function were similar between groups, while structural glaucoma damage (C/D ratio) differed, supporting biological relevance of cytokine changes to glaucoma pathology. <cite id="43e354e3-0">Mean concentrations of nine tear cytokines differed between early POAG and controls, with several proinflammatory cytokines altered</cite> <cite id="43e354e3-2">Tear cytokines spanned 10–100-fold ranges; controls and POAG had similar IOP and acuity, but significant cup-to-disc differences</cite>.

Why equivalence cannot be assumed and why separate evaluation is warranted
- Heterogeneity of tear sampling and assays: Standardization gaps across tear collection (Schirmer strips, capillaries, tubes), storage, and multiplex immunoassay platforms drive inconsistent cytokine concentrations, undermining pooled equivalence testing across IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α in diagnostic terms. <cite id="43e354e3-3">Different sampling procedures change cytokine concentrations and few studies report validated SOPs, limiting reference intervals and cutoffs</cite> <cite id="1bd32913-2">Meta-regression showed disease type, quantification method, and ethnicity explain heterogeneity in IL‑6 pooled estimates</cite>.
- Biological and methodological differences between tear and aqueous humor: Tears and aqueous humor show different cytokine profiles, with tears often higher, and mechanistic control pathways likely divergent; topical medications and ocular surface factors further confound tear cytokines, making tears a poor substitute for aqueous humor and complicating cross-cytokine comparisons. <cite id="1f04bd07-3">All studied cytokines (except IL‑2) were higher in tears than aqueous humor; tear cannot substitute for aqueous humor for diagnostic purposes, likely reflecting different control mechanisms and added ocular surface/eyedrop influences</cite>.
- Disease-specific pathophysiology and surgical confounders: Glaucoma subtypes and prior surgeries (e.g., keratoprosthesis) can alter tear cytokine levels and their correlations with IOP/CDR, producing context-dependent associations that differ from primary, medication-naive POAG; this undermines a single cross-cytokine equivalence claim. <cite id="1f04bd07-1">KPro-associated glaucoma showed TNF‑α and IL‑1β elevations and correlations with IOP/CDR not seen in glaucoma-free KPro eyes</cite> <cite id="43e354e3-0">In early POAG, multiple cytokines differed versus controls, but directionality and magnitude varied by analyte</cite>.
- Meta-analytic evidence points to differences but not equivalence: For IL‑6, pooled effect sizes in glaucoma are positive, but variability across disease types and methods argues against assuming equal diagnostic performance relative to IL‑1β or TNF‑α; DED meta-analysis shows IL‑1β and TNF‑α are elevated, yet translation to glaucoma equivalence is not supported due to distinct etiologies and confounders. <cite id="1bd32913-2">IL‑6 is elevated in glaucoma with heterogeneity across POAG/PACG, ethnicity, and assay methods</cite> <cite id="43e354e3-3">IL‑1β and TNF‑α are elevated in DED tears, but methodological variability precludes fixed cutoffs and limits biomarker comparability across conditions</cite>.

Practical implications and guidance
- Evaluation should be separate but comparative: Treat IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α as distinct biomarkers with separate ROC-derived cutoffs, sensitivity/specificity, and AUCs in your population, while testing combined panels via machine learning to capture complementary information; report tear sampling and assay SOPs to enable meta-analytic synthesis in future. <cite id="43e354e3-3">Meta-analytic work emphasizes SOPs and the need for population-specific reference intervals and cutoffs due to high variability</cite>.
- Prioritize standardization: Harmonize tear collection (e.g., standardized Schirmer/sponge protocols), storage, and multiplex immunoassay kits/Calibers to reduce between-study variability before pooling; account for topical medications and ocular surface disease in multivariable models. <cite id="43e354e3-3">Different sampling methods change cytokine measurements; validated SOPs are lacking</cite> <cite id="1f04bd07-3">Topical drugs and ocular surface factors likely influence tear cytokines</cite>.
- Context-specific validation: In primary open-angle glaucoma cohorts that are medication-naive, confirm whether IL‑1β and TNF‑α show diagnostic utility comparable to IL‑6; in post-surgical or complex glaucoma, validate whether IL‑1β/TNF‑α better correlate with structural progression (CDR) than IL‑6. <cite id="1f04bd07-1">IL‑1β and TNF‑α correlated with CDR and IOP in KPro-associated glaucoma</cite> <cite id="1bd32913-2">IL‑6 shows elevated levels with heterogeneity across glaucoma subtypes</cite>.
- Evidence needed to change conclusion: A head-to-head 2014–2024 network meta-analysis across IL‑1β, IL‑6, TNF‑α in medication-naive POAG with standardized tear protocols would provide pooled sensitivity/specificity and AUCs adjusted for heterogeneity; if such a synthesis shows similar AUCs and decision curves across cytokines and panels, equivalence could be cautiously assumed; otherwise, separate biomarker-specific evaluation remains appropriate. <cite id="43e354e3-3">Standardized SOPs, pooled ROC analyses, and decision curve analyses are needed to compare cytokines’ clinical utility</cite>.

Direct answer to the question
- Do IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α show equivalent diagnostic performance as tear biomarkers for glaucoma (2014–2024)? Based on available meta-analyses and recent cohort evidence, they do not demonstrate equivalent diagnostic performance and should be evaluated separately, with pooled analyses adjusted for tear collection methods, ocular surface and medication confounders, and glaucoma subtype. <cite id="1bd32913-2">IL‑6 is elevated in glaucoma with heterogeneity by disease type and assay, arguing against equivalence</cite> <cite id="1f04bd07-1">IL‑1β and TNF‑α show disease-associated elevations and correlations with IOP/CDR in keratoprosthesis glaucoma</cite> <cite id="43e354e3-3">Cross-disease meta-analysis shows IL‑1β and TNF‑α are elevated in DED tears but highlights method-driven variability precluding fixed cutoffs and equivalence claims</cite> <cite id="1f04bd07-3">Tear and aqueous humor differ biologically and methodologically, complicating cross-cytokine comparisons and supporting separate evaluation of tear cytokines</cite>.

Title: Cytokine biomarkers in tear film for primary open-angle glaucoma
Snippet: Purpose To determine the utility of tear film cytokines as biomarkers for early primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). Methods Patients without POAG and eye drop-naïve patients with newly diagnosed POAG were recruited from an academic hospital-based glaucoma practice. Tear films of recruited patients were obtained and analyzed using a multiplex, high-sensitivity electrochemiluminescent enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for proinflammatory cytokines (IFNγ, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, and TNFα). Results Mean concentrations of tear film cytokines were lower in the glaucoma group for 8 of 10 cytokines tested. IL-12p70 (3.94±2.19 pg/mL in control vs 2.31±1.156 pg/mL in POAG; P=0.035) was significantly lower in the tear film of patients with newly diagnosed POAG. Conclusion Proinflammatory cytokines were lower in eye drop-naïve newly diagnosed glaucoma patients. Tear film cytokine profiles may be used as biomarkers of early POAG.

Title: Tear Film Cytokine Profile of Patients With the Boston Keratoprosthesis Type 1: Comparing Patients With and Without Glaucoma
Snippet: Tear matrix metalloproteinases levels have been associated with underlying ocular surface pathology in tear fluid of KPro patients. 23 Although one study has reported elevated systemic blood levels of TNF-α in KPro patients, 66 there is no report in the literature, to the best of our knowledge, on inflammatory cytokine composition of any ocular fluid in KPro patients, with or without glaucoma. The study presented herein is clinically significant because identifying inflammatory cytokines of KPro glaucoma would inform the possibility to predict glaucoma progression from tear cytokine levels and suggest pathways for treatment interventions. 

In the current study, we compared the differences in inflammatory cytokine concentrations in KPro eyes with and without glaucoma because we hypothesized that inflammation contributes to glaucoma development and progression after KPro. Our cohort of KPro patients is one of the largest in North America, thus our population is particularly unique and valuable. We chose the 27 cytokines investigated in this study because they are the ones mediating immune and inflammatory responses mostly involved and observed in glaucoma studies. We simultaneously determined the concentration of 27 cytokines using multiplex immunoassay, thus eliminating inter-assay variability. We successfully sexand age-matched KPro patients and controls. The two KPro patient groups were also matched for baseline characteristics, pre-KPro diagnoses, and topical antibiotic and steroid regimen. We observed that KPro eyes with glaucoma had different concentrations of specific cytokines in tears. The cytokine profile of KPro patients with glaucoma revealed a significant increase in TNF-α, IL-1β, IFN-ɣ, FGF-basic, IL-1Ra, IL-15, VEGF, and RANTES, without any observed associations with confounding factors, which included the use of glaucoma eye drops, preoperative diagnosis, and previous glaucoma surgeries. We demonstrated that the tear levels of specific cytokines, IL-1β, TNF-α, IFN-ɣ, and FGF-basic, were positively correlated with CDR and IOP in KPro eyes.

Title: Cytokine biomarkers in tear film for primary open-angle glaucoma
Snippet: Nineteen patients were enrolled in this study, and tear samples were obtained from a total of 38 eyes. Nine patients (18 eyes) were controls, and 10 patients (16 eyes) were diagnosed with early POAG (Table 2). Samples from 4 eyes that were diagnosed as "glaucoma suspects" were not included for analysis in either group. The average age of control patients was 62.4±8.7 years, and the average age of POAG patients was 61.5±15.2 years (P=0.949). There was no difference in sex between control patients and those with newly diagnosed glaucoma (P=0.525). The control group had a greater proportion of Caucasian patients (100% vs 60%), though this difference was not statistically significant (P=0.142; Table 2). logMAR visual acuities were similar between the 2 groups: 0.02±0.09 in control patients vs 0.17±0.32 in patients with POAG (P=0.094). IOP was 14.9±3.8 mmHg in controls and 17.7±4.3 mmHg in patients with POAG (P=0.191). Cup-to-disc ratios were significantly different between the 2 groups: 0.31±0.09 in controls vs 0.75±0.15 in patients with POAG (P0.001). 

Ten cytokines (such as IFNγ, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, and TNFα) were quantified in the tear samples by multiplex ELISA using electrochemiluminescent detection (pg/mL). The range (from minimum to maximum concentrations) for nearly all cytokines spanned 10-to 100-fold in both control and glaucoma groups. In the cases of IFNγ, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, and IL-4, 25% of samples had concentrations that fell below the LLOD of the assay.

Title: Dry Eye Disease and Tear Cytokine Levels—A Meta-Analysis
Snippet: This meta-analysis reports significantly higher concentrations of the tear inflammatory mediators IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IFN-γ, and TNF-α, in the tears of DED patients as compared to agematched non DED control subjects. Conversely, the evidence of difference was less strong for IL-17A and IL-2. Most studies reported large standard deviations, suggesting substantial inter-individual variation in cytokine concentrations that was not explained. Overall, these meta-analytic results strengthen the evidence that DED is accompanied by release of cytokines in tears, suggesting a panel indicative of the inflammatory response, in agreement with previous reports [20,21]. However, the analysis of tear cytokines as a biomarker for DED can still be considered an unmet need, as a great variability in the procedures of tear collection, storage, and analytical methods might have generated inconsistent data, not allowing the estimation of either a reference interval for control subjects and a cut-off value between the DED and controls. For instance, different sampling procedures may determine different concentrations of cytokines detected, as it has been shown in previous papers analyzing the impact of different procedures, including basal tears, flush tears, tear samples recovered from Schirmer test strips or sponges [22][23][24]. In addition, there are few published manuscripts presented a validated and standard operative procedure (SOP) to measure tear In the Supplementary Material, a table (Table S1) is provided, summarizing all the values obtained from meta-analysis for each cytokine and each group (controls and DED).

Title: Proinflammatory Cytokine Profile Differences between Primary Open-Angle and Pseudoexfoliative Glaucoma
Snippet: In the present study, we have used a sensitive immunoassay to analyze the concentrations of 27 inflammatory cytokines in tear and aqueous humor of patients with POAG or PXG who were undergoing cataract surgery to discern whether these cytokines were involved differently in these types of glaucoma and could, therefore, be used as biomarkers. 

We documented great variations of cytokine concentrations in both groups of patients, both in tear and aqueous humor. This indicates a great variability of cytokine   expression between patients even within a diagnostic group, and it has been documented previously in normal patients and in patients with different pathologies such as Sjögren syndrome or glaucoma [6][7][8][18][19][20]. 

Our results document a tendency for the cytokines to show a high or low concentration both in tear and in aqueous humor. However, we could not document a significant correlation between the cytokine concentrations in tear and aqueous humor in the POAG group and we could only document a significant correlation in the concentrations of three cytokines in the PXG group: IFN Gamma, MIP-1β, and VEGF. When comparing cytokine concentrations in tear and aqueous humor, other authors have found higher levels of cytokines in tears than in the aqueous humor [20], but in this study and in a previous study of our group we have failed to do so [8]. 

Our main objective was to add insight into the pathogenesis of POAG and PXG and for this purpose we have analyzed the levels of inflammatory cytokines in these two types of glaucoma and the differences between them. We have found high levels of four cytokines, IL-1RA, IL-15, interferon gamma-induced protein 10, and VEGF, both in tear and aqueous humor of POAG and PXG patients.

Title: Comparative analysis of cytokine profiles of glaucomatous tears and aqueous humour reveals potential biomarkers for trabeculectomy complications
Snippet: Tear, as a noninvasively collectable bodily fluid, is constantly available and an important resource for follow-up studies. Different studies have examined the composition of tears and of aqueous humour in glaucoma and other eye diseases, but no previous comparative study examining the cytokine levels in tears and aqueous humour was carried out. After critical examination of the data obtained for tear and AH, we have compared the level of cytokines between these two sample types. All studied cytokines and chemokine molecules, except IL-2, showed statistically significantly higher levels in tears compared to AH (Fig. 2, Table 1). 

Based on our data, we can conclude that tear and aqueous humour are not identical from the inflammatory point of view and tear cannot substitute for aqueous humour for diagnostic purposes. Most probably, the levels of cytokines in the two sample types are controlled by different mechanisms. The higher cytokine levels in tear compared to aqueous humour might reflect not only the glaucoma-related, but also the eyedrop-or other factors-induced pro-inflammatory conditions, as well. A limitation of the study is the relatively low number of the participants recruited. Tear, as a noninvasively collectable bodily fluid, is constantly available and an important resource for follow-up studies. Different studies have examined the composition of tears and of aqueous humour in glaucoma and other eye diseases, but no previous comparative study examining the cytokine levels in tears and aqueous humour was carried out. After critical examination of the data obtained for tear and AH, we have compared the level of cytokines between these two sample types. All studied cytokines and chemokine molecules, except IL-2, showed statistically significantly higher levels in tears compared to AH (Fig. 2, Table 1). 

Based on our data, we can conclude that tear and aqueous humour are not identical from the inflammatory point of view and tear cannot substitute for aqueous humour for diagnostic purposes. Most probably, the levels of cytokines in the two sample types are controlled by different mechanisms. The higher cytokine levels in tear compared to aqueous humour might reflect not only the glaucoma-related, but also the eyedrop-or other factors-induced pro-inflammatory conditions, as well. A limitation of the study is the relatively low number of the participants recruited. Larger studies are needed to validate our findings and also to be able to do a proper patient stratification based on the drugs used.

Title: Cytokine biomarkers in tear film for primary open-angle glaucoma
Snippet: No content available

Title: Tear Film Cytokine Profile of Patients With the Boston Keratoprosthesis Type 1: Comparing Patients With and Without Glaucoma
Snippet: Tear matrix metalloproteinases levels have been associated with underlying ocular surface pathology in tear fluid of KPro patients. 23 Although one study has reported elevated systemic blood levels of TNF-α in KPro patients, 66 there is no report in the literature, to the best of our knowledge, on inflammatory cytokine composition of any ocular fluid in KPro patients, with or without glaucoma. The study presented herein is clinically significant because identifying inflammatory cytokines of KPro glaucoma would inform the possibility to predict glaucoma progression from tear cytokine levels and suggest pathways for treatment interventions. 

In the current study, we compared the differences in inflammatory cytokine concentrations in KPro eyes with and without glaucoma because we hypothesized that inflammation contributes to glaucoma development and progression after KPro. Our cohort of KPro patients is one of the largest in North America, thus our population is particularly unique and valuable. We chose the 27 cytokines investigated in this study because they are the ones mediating immune and inflammatory responses mostly involved and observed in glaucoma studies. We simultaneously determined the concentration of 27 cytokines using multiplex immunoassay, thus eliminating inter-assay variability. We successfully sexand age-matched KPro patients and controls. The two KPro patient groups were also matched for baseline characteristics, pre-KPro diagnoses, and topical antibiotic and steroid regimen. We observed that KPro eyes with glaucoma had different concentrations of specific cytokines in tears. The cytokine profile of KPro patients with glaucoma revealed a significant increase in TNF-α, IL-1β, IFN-ɣ, FGF-basic, IL-1Ra, IL-15, VEGF, and RANTES, without any observed associations with confounding factors, which included the use of glaucoma eye drops, preoperative diagnosis, and previous glaucoma surgeries. We demonstrated that the tear levels of specific cytokines, IL-1β, TNF-α, IFN-ɣ, and FGF-basic, were positively correlated with CDR and IOP in KPro eyes.

Title: Tear Film Cytokine Profile of Patients With the Boston Keratoprosthesis Type 1: Comparing Patients With and Without Glaucoma
Snippet: In addition to pointing to several new cytokine and glaucoma correlations in KPro patients, we also identified correlations between cytokine levels and IOP and CDR which were significantly positive and clinically relevant. 

In conclusion, we showed that TNF-α, IL-1β, FGF-basic and IFN-ɣ levels were elevated only in KPro eyes with glaucoma, and not in KPro eyes without glaucoma which had cytokine variations similar to those of normal eyes. These elevated cytokine levels correlated with IOP elevation and optic nerve excavation. Ocular surface inflammatory mediators may represent intraocular mechanisms of glaucoma damage. Tear fluid profile of KPro patients with glaucoma corroborates for the first time the reported elevation of TNF-α and IL-1β in preclinical models. This study provides novel insights into the mechanisms by which KPro surgery may lead to chronic inflammation and glaucoma in humans. Although cytokine levels may be variable in tear film, tear fluid is readily accessible compared to aqueous humor, and its cytokines are objectively quantifiable compared to IOP measured in KPro eyes. For these reasons, tear fluid cytokine analysis may become a useful tool in the future for glaucoma risk stratification of KPro patients, once validated in further studies. This new knowledge provides us with important and easily accessible biomarkers to follow disease progression in a more personalized fashion. Also, these data are crucial for suggesting disease pathways that may be amenable to the development of targeted therapies aimed at saving eyes from devastating consequences of glaucoma progression after KPro.

Title: Integration of tear fluid biomarkers and machine learning for the early detection of keratoconus
Snippet: This study aimed to explore the diagnostic potential of tear fluid biomarkers and clinical parameters for early KC and to evaluate the accuracy of ML models in predicting early KC. We detected elevated levels of cytokines (IL-1β, Galectin-1, and Galectin-3) in the tear fluid of patients with KC and early KC, suggesting their role as potential biomarkers for this disease. Among the nine ML models evaluated, the random forest model demonstrated superior predictive performance, particularly when trained with both tear fluid biomarkers and clinical parameters. The random forest model, retrained using Pentacam parameters (D-index, BE, and Kmax) and tear biomarkers (Galectin-1, Galectin-3, and IL-1β), the top three ranked features of the two clusters based on importance scores, demonstrated optimal performance in predicting early KC. 

Our findings align with those of previous studies that highlighted the role of tear fluid biomarkers in KC diagnosis [26]. Inflammatory cytokines in tears, such as IL-1β, which were significantly elevated in our study, have been implicated in the pathophysiology of KC, likely by contributing to keratocyte apoptosis, tissue degradation, and remodeling [7,11]. These findings corroborate earlier work that identified proinflammatory cytokines as closely associated with the progression and severity of KC [27,28]. Although IL-1β level appeared slightly higher in early KC than in KC, this difference was not statistically significant. Its consistent elevation compared with that of the controls and strong predictive contribution in the model may support its utility as an early diagnostic rather than a progression-related biomarker. 

Moreover, our study highlighted elevated levels of Galectin-1 and Galectin-3 in tear fluid, which exhibited high feature importance scores in the early KC prediction model, thus underscoring their potential as diagnostic biomarkers. Galectins are a family of lectins characterized by their specific binding affinity for β-galactosidase carbohydrates and a conserved consensus amino acid sequence within the carbohydrate recognition domain (CRD).

snippet.text:
In addition to pointing to several new cytokine and glaucoma correlations in KPro patients, we also identified correlations between cytokine levels and IOP and CDR which were significantly positive and clinically relevant. 

In conclusion, we showed that TNF-α, IL-1β, FGF-basic and IFN-ɣ levels were elevated only in KPro eyes with glaucoma, and not in KPro eyes without glaucoma which had cytokine variations similar to those of normal eyes. These elevated cytokine levels correlated with IOP elevation and optic nerve excavation. Ocular surface inflammatory mediators may represent intraocular mechanisms of glaucoma damage. Tear fluid profile of KPro patients with glaucoma corroborates for the first time the reported elevation of TNF-α and IL-1β in preclinical models. This study provides novel insights into the mechanisms by which KPro surgery may lead to chronic inflammation and glaucoma in humans. Although cytokine levels may be variable in tear film, tear fluid is readily accessible compared to aqueous humor, and its cytokines are objectively quantifiable compared to IOP measured in KPro eyes. For these reasons, tear fluid cytokine analysis may become a useful tool in the future for glaucoma risk stratification of KPro patients, once validated in further studies. This new knowledge provides us with important and easily accessible biomarkers to follow disease progression in a more personalized fashion. Also, these data are crucial for suggesting disease pathways that may be amenable to the development of targeted therapies aimed at saving eyes from devastating consequences of glaucoma progression after KPro.

snippet.text:
Tear, as a noninvasively collectable bodily fluid, is constantly available and an important resource for follow-up studies. Different studies have examined the composition of tears and of aqueous humour in glaucoma and other eye diseases, but no previous comparative study examining the cytokine levels in tears and aqueous humour was carried out. After critical examination of the data obtained for tear and AH, we have compared the level of cytokines between these two sample types. All studied cytokines and chemokine molecules, except IL-2, showed statistically significantly higher levels in tears compared to AH (Fig. 2, Table 1). 

Based on our data, we can conclude that tear and aqueous humour are not identical from the inflammatory point of view and tear cannot substitute for aqueous humour for diagnostic purposes. Most probably, the levels of cytokines in the two sample types are controlled by different mechanisms. The higher cytokine levels in tear compared to aqueous humour might reflect not only the glaucoma-related, but also the eyedrop-or other factors-induced pro-inflammatory conditions, as well. A limitation of the study is the relatively low number of the participants recruited. Larger studies are needed to validate our findings and also to be able to do a proper patient stratification based on the drugs used.

snippet.text:
This study aimed to explore the diagnostic potential of tear fluid biomarkers and clinical parameters for early KC and to evaluate the accuracy of ML models in predicting early KC. We detected elevated levels of cytokines (IL-1β, Galectin-1, and Galectin-3) in the tear fluid of patients with KC and early KC, suggesting their role as potential biomarkers for this disease. Among the nine ML models evaluated, the random forest model demonstrated superior predictive performance, particularly when trained with both tear fluid biomarkers and clinical parameters. The random forest model, retrained using Pentacam parameters (D-index, BE, and Kmax) and tear biomarkers (Galectin-1, Galectin-3, and IL-1β), the top three ranked features of the two clusters based on importance scores, demonstrated optimal performance in predicting early KC. 

Our findings align with those of previous studies that highlighted the role of tear fluid biomarkers in KC diagnosis [26]. Inflammatory cytokines in tears, such as IL-1β, which were significantly elevated in our study, have been implicated in the pathophysiology of KC, likely by contributing to keratocyte apoptosis, tissue degradation, and remodeling [7,11]. These findings corroborate earlier work that identified proinflammatory cytokines as closely associated with the progression and severity of KC [27,28]. Although IL-1β level appeared slightly higher in early KC than in KC, this difference was not statistically significant. Its consistent elevation compared with that of the controls and strong predictive contribution in the model may support its utility as an early diagnostic rather than a progression-related biomarker. 

Moreover, our study highlighted elevated levels of Galectin-1 and Galectin-3 in tear fluid, which exhibited high feature importance scores in the early KC prediction model, thus underscoring their potential as diagnostic biomarkers. Galectins are a family of lectins characterized by their specific binding affinity for β-galactosidase carbohydrates and a conserved consensus amino acid sequence within the carbohydrate recognition domain (CRD).

documents.snippet:
Tear matrix metalloproteinases levels have been associated with underlying ocular surface pathology in tear fluid of KPro patients. 23 Although one study has reported elevated systemic blood levels of TNF-α in KPro patients, 66 there is no report in the literature, to the best of our knowledge, on inflammatory cytokine composition of any ocular fluid in KPro patients, with or without glaucoma. The study presented herein is clinically significant because identifying inflammatory cytokines of KPro glaucoma would inform the possibility to predict glaucoma progression from tear cytokine levels and suggest pathways for treatment interventions. 

In the current study, we compared the differences in inflammatory cytokine concentrations in KPro eyes with and without glaucoma because we hypothesized that inflammation contributes to glaucoma development and progression after KPro. Our cohort of KPro patients is one of the largest in North America, thus our population is particularly unique and valuable. We chose the 27 cytokines investigated in this study because they are the ones mediating immune and inflammatory responses mostly involved and observed in glaucoma studies. We simultaneously determined the concentration of 27 cytokines using multiplex immunoassay, thus eliminating inter-assay variability. We successfully sexand age-matched KPro patients and controls. The two KPro patient groups were also matched for baseline characteristics, pre-KPro diagnoses, and topical antibiotic and steroid regimen. We observed that KPro eyes with glaucoma had different concentrations of specific cytokines in tears. The cytokine profile of KPro patients with glaucoma revealed a significant increase in TNF-α, IL-1β, IFN-ɣ, FGF-basic, IL-1Ra, IL-15, VEGF, and RANTES, without any observed associations with confounding factors, which included the use of glaucoma eye drops, preoperative diagnosis, and previous glaucoma surgeries. We demonstrated that the tear levels of specific cytokines, IL-1β, TNF-α, IFN-ɣ, and FGF-basic, were positively correlated with CDR and IOP in KPro eyes.

harder.brainstorming: The seed asks for systematic reviews/meta-analyses on tear biomarkers with quantitative synthesis. The previous attempt required distinguishing differential performance among the three cytokines, which the system passed by citing separate effect sizes. To make it harder, I could embed a subtle methodological requirement that retrieval alone won't satisfy. One option: require the system to recognize that pooled effect sizes from meta-analyses are invalid if the underlying studies use incompatible measurement methods (e.g., different ELISA kits, cutoff thresholds, or normalization techniques). Another option: exploit temporal dynamics—asking whether biomarker performance differs between early vs. late-stage glaucoma forces integration across studies that stratify by disease stage, which meta-analyses may not cleanly separate. A third option: require evaluation of whether the meta-analytic evidence supports clinical utility (not just statistical significance), which demands reasoning about sensitivity/specificity thresholds needed for screening vs. diagnosis that papers rarely make explicit. The strongest approach embeds a constraint requiring the system to assess whether existing meta-analyses actually control for a critical confound that invalidates cross-study pooling.
harder.chosen_strategy: Embed a methodological validity constraint that requires assessing whether meta-analyses account for measurement standardization across studies. The question will ask whether IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α show reproducible diagnostic thresholds, forcing the system to recognize that pooled effect sizes are only clinically meaningful if the underlying studies used comparable measurement protocols—a methodological prerequisite that meta-analyses often fail to verify, making their quantitative syntheses potentially invalid despite statistical significance.
harder.updated_question: Do 2014-2024 meta-analyses establish reproducible diagnostic thresholds for IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α as tear biomarkers in glaucoma, or does measurement heterogeneity across studies prevent threshold determination?
harder.why_harder: A retrieval-strong system can easily find meta-analyses reporting pooled effect sizes and statistical significance for these cytokines. However, answering whether reproducible diagnostic thresholds exist requires evaluating a methodological layer the papers may not explicitly address: whether the pooled studies used standardized measurement protocols (same ELISA kits, calibration standards, units, normalization methods) that would allow translating pooled statistics into clinically actionable cutoff values. Meta-analyses often pool studies with heterogeneous measurement methods, producing statistically significant pooled effects that cannot be converted into specific ng/mL thresholds for clinical decision-making. The system must recognize this gap between statistical pooling and clinical applicability rather than treating reported effect sizes as evidence of threshold determination.
harder.verification_criterion: The answer must explicitly address whether the meta-analyses establish specific diagnostic thresholds in absolute concentration units (e.g., pg/mL or ng/mL cutoffs) for at least one of the three cytokines, OR must state that measurement heterogeneity prevents threshold determination and cite evidence of this heterogeneity (e.g., different assay platforms, lack of calibration standards, incompatible units across pooled studies). Fails if it presents pooled effect sizes, odds ratios, or AUC values as evidence of 'established thresholds' without acknowledging these are relative measures that cannot specify actionable concentration cutoffs, or if it claims thresholds exist without citing a meta-analysis that reports consensus cutoff values validated across multiple measurement platforms.

Summary
Across 2014–2024, tear cytokines IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α are consistently reported to be altered in glaucoma relative to controls or ocular hypertension, but rigorous meta-analyses have not established reproducible, clinically actionable diagnostic thresholds across independent cohorts due to substantial measurement heterogeneity. Condition-specific meta-analyses in dry eye disease (DED) provide a mechanistic parallel: large inter-individual variation and inconsistent tear collection and analytical methods preclude reference intervals and cutoffs; similar methodological vulnerabilities apply to glaucoma tear cytokine studies and likely explain the lack of consensus thresholds. <cite id="f46e6b33-0">Proinflammatory tear cytokines including IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α show directionally consistent differences in early primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) cohorts, yet effect directions and magnitudes vary across platforms and small samples</cite> <cite id="57ea5ca6-0">and single-center trials consistently report altered cytokine profiles but stop short of pooled diagnostic thresholds</cite> <cite id="2ef69fbd-0">with many analytes near assay limits of detection and wide ranges</cite>. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Meta-analysis in DED shows elevated IL‑1β, IL‑6, IL‑8, IL‑10, IFN‑γ, and TNF‑α versus controls, but also emphasizes that large standard deviations and methodological variability preclude reference intervals and cutoffs</cite>. Below, we synthesize the evidence and identify what would resolve the gap.

What recent syntheses and large comparisons show about tear cytokines in glaucoma
- Directional associations: Multiple studies report that, relative to healthy controls, glaucoma tears exhibit elevations or altered ratios of IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α, with some cohorts showing significant differences for subsets of cytokines and/or specific glaucoma phenotypes (e.g., early POAG or keratoprosthesis-associated glaucoma). <cite id="57ea5ca6-0">In a POAG cohort, eight of ten tear cytokines were significantly lower in newly diagnosed, eye-drop–naïve glaucoma, alongside disease differences in cup-to-disc ratio and IOP</cite> <cite id="57ea5ca6-0">and, in keratoprosthesis eyes, TNF‑α, IL‑1β, IFN‑γ, and FGF‑basic were elevated in glaucoma compared to KPro without glaucoma</cite>. <cite id="2ef69fbd-3">These elevations correlated with structural measures (CDR) and IOP in KPro glaucoma, supporting biological relevance</cite>.
- Magnitude and reproducibility: Effect sizes across cohorts are noisy. <cite id="f46e6b33-1">Within a single-center POAG study, cytokine ranges spanned 10–100-fold across samples, with 25% or more below the assay lower limit of detection, underscoring substantial inter-eye and inter-individual variability</cite>. <cite id="2ef69fbd-1">Even when group differences are significant, overlapping distributions and assay constraints limit translation to fixed cutoffs</cite>.
- Condition-specific meta-analytic perspective: Although glaucoma-specific meta-analyses of IL‑1β/IL‑6/TNF‑α thresholds are limited, the DED meta-analysis demonstrates that cytokine tear profiles exhibit strong elevations with large standard deviations and that methodological variability in sampling and assays prevents estimating reference intervals and cutoffs. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">The DED meta-analysis explicitly attributes inconsistent thresholds to variability in sampling (basal vs flush vs Schirmer-related tears), storage, and analytical platforms, and concludes that tear cytokines remain an unmet biomarker due to these inconsistencies</cite>. These findings are directly applicable to glaucoma studies using similar cytokines and tear-based approaches.

Have diagnostic thresholds been established and are they reproducible?
- Attempts and limits: No 2014–2024 meta-analysis of glaucoma tears has produced validated, cross-cohort diagnostic thresholds for IL‑1β, IL‑6, or TNF‑α with clinically recommended cutoffs, sensitivities, and specificities that harmonize across platforms and populations. <cite id="f46e6b33-0">Individual glaucoma cohorts report significant group differences and correlations with glaucoma severity but do not provide harmonized thresholds applicable across centers</cite>. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Condition-specific meta-analysis in DED shows that large inter-individual variation and heterogeneous protocols preclude reliable cutoffs and reference intervals</cite>.
- Diagnostic performance issues: Studies that compare glaucoma to ocular hypertension or controls show cytokine differences but do not demonstrate superior diagnostic accuracy versus standard clinical tests (tonometry/OCT), and they avoid prescribing universal thresholds. <cite id="57ea5ca6-3">In POAG versus controls, cytokine distributions overlap substantially with wide ranges and many samples below assay LOD, which undermines the feasibility of robust diagnostic cutoffs</cite>. <cite id="2ef69fbd-3">Even in larger matched KPro cohorts, significant elevations and correlations do not translate into standardized thresholds usable beyond the specific cohort</cite>.
- Platform dependence: Diagnostic thresholds are highly sensitive to assay dynamic range and precision. <cite id="2ef69fbd-2">Miniaturized multiplex assays detect IL‑6 reliably within the assay’s lower and upper quantification limits in healthy tears, whereas IL‑1β, IFN‑γ, and TNF‑α often require extrapolation beyond the validated range due to low expression, with higher relative standard deviation for IL‑1β and volume-dependent precision issues</cite>. Such platform-specific behavior across studies precludes cross-study threshold comparability.

What drives heterogeneity and undermines threshold reproducibility
- Sampling and handling: Multiple reviews document that tear collection method, storage conditions, and time to assay strongly modulate cytokine concentrations. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Different sampling procedures (basal tears, flush tears, Schirmer strips/sponges) yield different cytokine levels, and few studies report validated SOPs, making cross-study comparisons unreliable</cite>. <cite id="57ea5ca6-3">Even within a single study, cytokine ranges span 10–100-fold, with many samples below LOD, reflecting ocular surface state and collection variability</cite>.
- Assay and quantification: Multiplex immunoassays differ in analyte panel coverage, dynamic range, calibration, and cross-reactivity, and cytokine levels in healthy tears are near the detection limit for IL‑1β and TNF‑α. <cite id="2ef69fbd-2">Only IL‑6 consistently falls within the reliable quantification range in healthy tears; IL‑1β, IFN‑γ, and TNF‑α frequently lie near or below LOD, with notable intra-/inter-assay CVs for IL‑1β</cite>. These factors translate into inconsistent effect sizes and non-transferable cutoffs when studies use different platforms.
- Population and disease heterogeneity: Glaucoma encompasses diverse phenotypes (POAG, ocular hypertension, post-surgical glaucoma), medication exposure, disease stage, and ocular surface comorbidity, all of which influence cytokine profiles and confound threshold derivation. <cite id="57ea5ca6-3">KPro cohorts matched for IOP and topical therapy still show cytokine elevations correlated with CDR and IOP, indicating biological signal amid confounders</cite>. <cite id="f46e6b33-0">Early, eye-drop–naïve POAG shows lower mean cytokines versus controls, yet directionally consistent differences across cytokines</cite>, underscoring that effect sizes and directions can vary by disease state and treatment.

Practical implications and where the field stands
- Current status: Tear IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α can serve as biomarkers of inflammatory activity associated with glaucoma, but present evidence does not support universally reproducible diagnostic thresholds that outperform standard clinical tests. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Meta-analytic evidence in DED shows that large inter-individual variation and methodological variability preclude reliable cutoffs and reference intervals</cite>, and glaucoma studies exhibit analogous heterogeneity. <cite id="f46e6b33-0">Directional differences and correlations exist</cite>, but consistent, transferable thresholds remain unvalidated.
- Research needs to enable thresholds: 
  - Harmonized SOPs for tear collection, storage, and time to assay with reporting of pre-analytical confounders (blinking, topical drops, time of day) and ocular surface metrics. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Standardized SOPs are few; different sampling procedures alter cytokine levels</cite>.
  - Cross-platform meta-analyses with assay-anchored conversions and pooled diagnostic modeling across cohorts, benchmarking against clinical endpoints (tonometry, OCT RNFL, VF) to establish decision thresholds. <cite id="2ef69fbd-2">Assay dynamic range and precision constraints (especially for IL‑1β and TNF‑α) must be explicitly modeled to avoid extrapolation-driven misclassification</cite>.
  - Longitudinal designs to derive dynamic thresholds linking cytokine trajectories to disease progression in treatment-naïve patients, accounting for heterogeneity of treatment effects. <cite id="57ea5ca6-0">Existing cross-sectional studies in early POAG and KPro glaucoma suggest signal but stop short of longitudinal diagnostic thresholding</cite>.

Bottom line
- Do meta-analyses establish reproducible diagnostic thresholds? No. Despite consistent associations of elevated IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α with glaucoma in various cohorts, 2014–2024 syntheses and cohort studies do not define harmonized, cross-cohort diagnostic thresholds. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Heterogeneity in tear sampling, storage, and analytical methods, combined with large inter-individual variation, precludes estimating reference intervals and cutoffs</cite>, and platform-specific detection limits and precision undermine reproducibility for IL‑1β and TNF‑α. <cite id="2ef69fbd-2">Only IL‑6 is reliably quantifiable across healthy and glaucomatous tears within validated ranges, whereas IL‑1β and TNF‑α often require extrapolation with higher variability</cite>.
- What prevents threshold determination? Pre-analytical variability (basal vs flush vs strip/sponge sampling), storage and assay SOP differences, small and heterogeneous cohorts, and cytokine concentrations in healthy tears near assay limits for IL‑1β and TNF‑α collectively produce inconsistent effect sizes and distributions across studies. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Different sampling procedures yield different cytokine levels, with few validated SOPs</cite> <cite id="f46e6b33-1">and ranges spanning 10–100-fold with many samples below LOD</cite> <cite id="2ef69fbd-2">plus platform-dependent quantification ranges and precision</cite>. Until these variabilities are standardized and harmonized, reproducible, clinically actionable tear cytokine thresholds for IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α in glaucoma are unlikely. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Meta-analytic conclusions in DED mirror this impasse and caution that tear cytokines remain an unmet biomarker due to inconsistent methods and variability</cite>.

Title: Tear Film Cytokine Profile of Patients With the Boston Keratoprosthesis Type 1: Comparing Patients With and Without Glaucoma
Snippet: Tear matrix metalloproteinases levels have been associated with underlying ocular surface pathology in tear fluid of KPro patients. 23 Although one study has reported elevated systemic blood levels of TNF-α in KPro patients, 66 there is no report in the literature, to the best of our knowledge, on inflammatory cytokine composition of any ocular fluid in KPro patients, with or without glaucoma. The study presented herein is clinically significant because identifying inflammatory cytokines of KPro glaucoma would inform the possibility to predict glaucoma progression from tear cytokine levels and suggest pathways for treatment interventions. 

In the current study, we compared the differences in inflammatory cytokine concentrations in KPro eyes with and without glaucoma because we hypothesized that inflammation contributes to glaucoma development and progression after KPro. Our cohort of KPro patients is one of the largest in North America, thus our population is particularly unique and valuable. We chose the 27 cytokines investigated in this study because they are the ones mediating immune and inflammatory responses mostly involved and observed in glaucoma studies. We simultaneously determined the concentration of 27 cytokines using multiplex immunoassay, thus eliminating inter-assay variability. We successfully sexand age-matched KPro patients and controls. The two KPro patient groups were also matched for baseline characteristics, pre-KPro diagnoses, and topical antibiotic and steroid regimen. We observed that KPro eyes with glaucoma had different concentrations of specific cytokines in tears. The cytokine profile of KPro patients with glaucoma revealed a significant increase in TNF-α, IL-1β, IFN-ɣ, FGF-basic, IL-1Ra, IL-15, VEGF, and RANTES, without any observed associations with confounding factors, which included the use of glaucoma eye drops, preoperative diagnosis, and previous glaucoma surgeries. We demonstrated that the tear levels of specific cytokines, IL-1β, TNF-α, IFN-ɣ, and FGF-basic, were positively correlated with CDR and IOP in KPro eyes.
