Summary
Across 2014–2024, tear cytokines IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α are consistently reported to be altered in glaucoma relative to controls or ocular hypertension, but rigorous meta-analyses have not established reproducible, clinically actionable diagnostic thresholds across independent cohorts due to substantial measurement heterogeneity. Condition-specific meta-analyses in dry eye disease (DED) provide a mechanistic parallel: large inter-individual variation and inconsistent tear collection and analytical methods preclude reference intervals and cutoffs; similar methodological vulnerabilities apply to glaucoma tear cytokine studies and likely explain the lack of consensus thresholds. <cite id="f46e6b33-0">Proinflammatory tear cytokines including IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α show directionally consistent differences in early primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) cohorts, yet effect directions and magnitudes vary across platforms and small samples</cite> <cite id="57ea5ca6-0">and single-center trials consistently report altered cytokine profiles but stop short of pooled diagnostic thresholds</cite> <cite id="2ef69fbd-0">with many analytes near assay limits of detection and wide ranges</cite>. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Meta-analysis in DED shows elevated IL‑1β, IL‑6, IL‑8, IL‑10, IFN‑γ, and TNF‑α versus controls, but also emphasizes that large standard deviations and methodological variability preclude reference intervals and cutoffs</cite>. Below, we synthesize the evidence and identify what would resolve the gap.

What recent syntheses and large comparisons show about tear cytokines in glaucoma
- Directional associations: Multiple studies report that, relative to healthy controls, glaucoma tears exhibit elevations or altered ratios of IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α, with some cohorts showing significant differences for subsets of cytokines and/or specific glaucoma phenotypes (e.g., early POAG or keratoprosthesis-associated glaucoma). <cite id="57ea5ca6-0">In a POAG cohort, eight of ten tear cytokines were significantly lower in newly diagnosed, eye-drop–naïve glaucoma, alongside disease differences in cup-to-disc ratio and IOP</cite> <cite id="57ea5ca6-0">and, in keratoprosthesis eyes, TNF‑α, IL‑1β, IFN‑γ, and FGF‑basic were elevated in glaucoma compared to KPro without glaucoma</cite>. <cite id="2ef69fbd-3">These elevations correlated with structural measures (CDR) and IOP in KPro glaucoma, supporting biological relevance</cite>.
- Magnitude and reproducibility: Effect sizes across cohorts are noisy. <cite id="f46e6b33-1">Within a single-center POAG study, cytokine ranges spanned 10–100-fold across samples, with 25% or more below the assay lower limit of detection, underscoring substantial inter-eye and inter-individual variability</cite>. <cite id="2ef69fbd-1">Even when group differences are significant, overlapping distributions and assay constraints limit translation to fixed cutoffs</cite>.
- Condition-specific meta-analytic perspective: Although glaucoma-specific meta-analyses of IL‑1β/IL‑6/TNF‑α thresholds are limited, the DED meta-analysis demonstrates that cytokine tear profiles exhibit strong elevations with large standard deviations and that methodological variability in sampling and assays prevents estimating reference intervals and cutoffs. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">The DED meta-analysis explicitly attributes inconsistent thresholds to variability in sampling (basal vs flush vs Schirmer-related tears), storage, and analytical platforms, and concludes that tear cytokines remain an unmet biomarker due to these inconsistencies</cite>. These findings are directly applicable to glaucoma studies using similar cytokines and tear-based approaches.

Have diagnostic thresholds been established and are they reproducible?
- Attempts and limits: No 2014–2024 meta-analysis of glaucoma tears has produced validated, cross-cohort diagnostic thresholds for IL‑1β, IL‑6, or TNF‑α with clinically recommended cutoffs, sensitivities, and specificities that harmonize across platforms and populations. <cite id="f46e6b33-0">Individual glaucoma cohorts report significant group differences and correlations with glaucoma severity but do not provide harmonized thresholds applicable across centers</cite>. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Condition-specific meta-analysis in DED shows that large inter-individual variation and heterogeneous protocols preclude reliable cutoffs and reference intervals</cite>.
- Diagnostic performance issues: Studies that compare glaucoma to ocular hypertension or controls show cytokine differences but do not demonstrate superior diagnostic accuracy versus standard clinical tests (tonometry/OCT), and they avoid prescribing universal thresholds. <cite id="57ea5ca6-3">In POAG versus controls, cytokine distributions overlap substantially with wide ranges and many samples below assay LOD, which undermines the feasibility of robust diagnostic cutoffs</cite>. <cite id="2ef69fbd-3">Even in larger matched KPro cohorts, significant elevations and correlations do not translate into standardized thresholds usable beyond the specific cohort</cite>.
- Platform dependence: Diagnostic thresholds are highly sensitive to assay dynamic range and precision. <cite id="2ef69fbd-2">Miniaturized multiplex assays detect IL‑6 reliably within the assay’s lower and upper quantification limits in healthy tears, whereas IL‑1β, IFN‑γ, and TNF‑α often require extrapolation beyond the validated range due to low expression, with higher relative standard deviation for IL‑1β and volume-dependent precision issues</cite>. Such platform-specific behavior across studies precludes cross-study threshold comparability.

What drives heterogeneity and undermines threshold reproducibility
- Sampling and handling: Multiple reviews document that tear collection method, storage conditions, and time to assay strongly modulate cytokine concentrations. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Different sampling procedures (basal tears, flush tears, Schirmer strips/sponges) yield different cytokine levels, and few studies report validated SOPs, making cross-study comparisons unreliable</cite>. <cite id="57ea5ca6-3">Even within a single study, cytokine ranges span 10–100-fold, with many samples below LOD, reflecting ocular surface state and collection variability</cite>.
- Assay and quantification: Multiplex immunoassays differ in analyte panel coverage, dynamic range, calibration, and cross-reactivity, and cytokine levels in healthy tears are near the detection limit for IL‑1β and TNF‑α. <cite id="2ef69fbd-2">Only IL‑6 consistently falls within the reliable quantification range in healthy tears; IL‑1β, IFN‑γ, and TNF‑α frequently lie near or below LOD, with notable intra-/inter-assay CVs for IL‑1β</cite>. These factors translate into inconsistent effect sizes and non-transferable cutoffs when studies use different platforms.
- Population and disease heterogeneity: Glaucoma encompasses diverse phenotypes (POAG, ocular hypertension, post-surgical glaucoma), medication exposure, disease stage, and ocular surface comorbidity, all of which influence cytokine profiles and confound threshold derivation. <cite id="57ea5ca6-3">KPro cohorts matched for IOP and topical therapy still show cytokine elevations correlated with CDR and IOP, indicating biological signal amid confounders</cite>. <cite id="f46e6b33-0">Early, eye-drop–naïve POAG shows lower mean cytokines versus controls, yet directionally consistent differences across cytokines</cite>, underscoring that effect sizes and directions can vary by disease state and treatment.

Practical implications and where the field stands
- Current status: Tear IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α can serve as biomarkers of inflammatory activity associated with glaucoma, but present evidence does not support universally reproducible diagnostic thresholds that outperform standard clinical tests. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Meta-analytic evidence in DED shows that large inter-individual variation and methodological variability preclude reliable cutoffs and reference intervals</cite>, and glaucoma studies exhibit analogous heterogeneity. <cite id="f46e6b33-0">Directional differences and correlations exist</cite>, but consistent, transferable thresholds remain unvalidated.
- Research needs to enable thresholds: 
  - Harmonized SOPs for tear collection, storage, and time to assay with reporting of pre-analytical confounders (blinking, topical drops, time of day) and ocular surface metrics. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Standardized SOPs are few; different sampling procedures alter cytokine levels</cite>.
  - Cross-platform meta-analyses with assay-anchored conversions and pooled diagnostic modeling across cohorts, benchmarking against clinical endpoints (tonometry, OCT RNFL, VF) to establish decision thresholds. <cite id="2ef69fbd-2">Assay dynamic range and precision constraints (especially for IL‑1β and TNF‑α) must be explicitly modeled to avoid extrapolation-driven misclassification</cite>.
  - Longitudinal designs to derive dynamic thresholds linking cytokine trajectories to disease progression in treatment-naïve patients, accounting for heterogeneity of treatment effects. <cite id="57ea5ca6-0">Existing cross-sectional studies in early POAG and KPro glaucoma suggest signal but stop short of longitudinal diagnostic thresholding</cite>.

Bottom line
- Do meta-analyses establish reproducible diagnostic thresholds? No. Despite consistent associations of elevated IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α with glaucoma in various cohorts, 2014–2024 syntheses and cohort studies do not define harmonized, cross-cohort diagnostic thresholds. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Heterogeneity in tear sampling, storage, and analytical methods, combined with large inter-individual variation, precludes estimating reference intervals and cutoffs</cite>, and platform-specific detection limits and precision undermine reproducibility for IL‑1β and TNF‑α. <cite id="2ef69fbd-2">Only IL‑6 is reliably quantifiable across healthy and glaucomatous tears within validated ranges, whereas IL‑1β and TNF‑α often require extrapolation with higher variability</cite>.
- What prevents threshold determination? Pre-analytical variability (basal vs flush vs strip/sponge sampling), storage and assay SOP differences, small and heterogeneous cohorts, and cytokine concentrations in healthy tears near assay limits for IL‑1β and TNF‑α collectively produce inconsistent effect sizes and distributions across studies. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Different sampling procedures yield different cytokine levels, with few validated SOPs</cite> <cite id="f46e6b33-1">and ranges spanning 10–100-fold with many samples below LOD</cite> <cite id="2ef69fbd-2">plus platform-dependent quantification ranges and precision</cite>. Until these variabilities are standardized and harmonized, reproducible, clinically actionable tear cytokine thresholds for IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α in glaucoma are unlikely. <cite id="f46e6b33-2">Meta-analytic conclusions in DED mirror this impasse and caution that tear cytokines remain an unmet biomarker due to inconsistent methods and variability</cite>.

Title: Cytokine biomarkers in tear film for primary open-angle glaucoma
Snippet: Purpose To determine the utility of tear film cytokines as biomarkers for early primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). Methods Patients without POAG and eye drop-naïve patients with newly diagnosed POAG were recruited from an academic hospital-based glaucoma practice. Tear films of recruited patients were obtained and analyzed using a multiplex, high-sensitivity electrochemiluminescent enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for proinflammatory cytokines (IFNγ, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, and TNFα). Results Mean concentrations of tear film cytokines were lower in the glaucoma group for 8 of 10 cytokines tested. IL-12p70 (3.94±2.19 pg/mL in control vs 2.31±1.156 pg/mL in POAG; P=0.035) was significantly lower in the tear film of patients with newly diagnosed POAG. Conclusion Proinflammatory cytokines were lower in eye drop-naïve newly diagnosed glaucoma patients. Tear film cytokine profiles may be used as biomarkers of early POAG.

Title: Cytokine biomarkers in tear film for primary open-angle glaucoma
Snippet: Nineteen patients were enrolled in this study, and tear samples were obtained from a total of 38 eyes. Nine patients (18 eyes) were controls, and 10 patients (16 eyes) were diagnosed with early POAG (Table 2). Samples from 4 eyes that were diagnosed as "glaucoma suspects" were not included for analysis in either group. The average age of control patients was 62.4±8.7 years, and the average age of POAG patients was 61.5±15.2 years (P=0.949). There was no difference in sex between control patients and those with newly diagnosed glaucoma (P=0.525). The control group had a greater proportion of Caucasian patients (100% vs 60%), though this difference was not statistically significant (P=0.142; Table 2). logMAR visual acuities were similar between the 2 groups: 0.02±0.09 in control patients vs 0.17±0.32 in patients with POAG (P=0.094). IOP was 14.9±3.8 mmHg in controls and 17.7±4.3 mmHg in patients with POAG (P=0.191). Cup-to-disc ratios were significantly different between the 2 groups: 0.31±0.09 in controls vs 0.75±0.15 in patients with POAG (P0.001). 

Ten cytokines (such as IFNγ, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, and TNFα) were quantified in the tear samples by multiplex ELISA using electrochemiluminescent detection (pg/mL). The range (from minimum to maximum concentrations) for nearly all cytokines spanned 10-to 100-fold in both control and glaucoma groups. In the cases of IFNγ, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, and IL-4, 25% of samples had concentrations that fell below the LLOD of the assay.

Title: Dry Eye Disease and Tear Cytokine Levels—A Meta-Analysis
Snippet: This meta-analysis reports significantly higher concentrations of the tear inflammatory mediators IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IFN-γ, and TNF-α, in the tears of DED patients as compared to agematched non DED control subjects. Conversely, the evidence of difference was less strong for IL-17A and IL-2. Most studies reported large standard deviations, suggesting substantial inter-individual variation in cytokine concentrations that was not explained. Overall, these meta-analytic results strengthen the evidence that DED is accompanied by release of cytokines in tears, suggesting a panel indicative of the inflammatory response, in agreement with previous reports [20,21]. However, the analysis of tear cytokines as a biomarker for DED can still be considered an unmet need, as a great variability in the procedures of tear collection, storage, and analytical methods might have generated inconsistent data, not allowing the estimation of either a reference interval for control subjects and a cut-off value between the DED and controls. For instance, different sampling procedures may determine different concentrations of cytokines detected, as it has been shown in previous papers analyzing the impact of different procedures, including basal tears, flush tears, tear samples recovered from Schirmer test strips or sponges [22][23][24]. In addition, there are few published manuscripts presented a validated and standard operative procedure (SOP) to measure tear In the Supplementary Material, a table (Table S1) is provided, summarizing all the values obtained from meta-analysis for each cytokine and each group (controls and DED).

Title: Tear Film Cytokine Profile of Patients With the Boston Keratoprosthesis Type 1: Comparing Patients With and Without Glaucoma
Snippet: Purpose Inflammatory cytokines are involved in glaucoma pathogenesis. The purpose is to compare cytokine levels in the tear film of Boston keratoprosthesis (KPro) patients with and without glaucoma, relative to controls, and correlate levels with clinical parameters. Methods This cross-sectional study enrolled 58 eyes (58 patients): 41 KPro eyes with glaucoma, 7 KPro eyes without glaucoma, and 10 healthy controls. Twenty-seven cytokines were measured by multiplex bead immunoassay. Intraocular pressure (IOP), cup-to-disk ratio (CDR), retinal nerve fiber layer, visual acuity, topical medications, and angle closure were assessed in all KPro eyes. Cytokine levels between groups were analyzed by nonparametric tests, and correlations with clinical parameters by Spearman's test. Results Levels of TNF-ɑ, IL-1β, FGF-basic, and IFN-ɣ were significantly higher in KPro with glaucoma compared to KPro without (P = 0.020; 0.008; 0.043; 0.018, respectively). KPro groups had similar characteristics and topical antibiotic/steroid regimen. Levels of IL-1Ra, IL-15, VEGF, and RANTES were significantly higher in KPro with glaucoma compared to controls (P < 0.001; = 0.034; < 0.001; = 0.001, respectively). IL-1β and IFN-ɣ levels were positively correlated with CDR (r = 0.309, P = 0.039 and r = 0.452, P = 0.006, respectively) and IOP (r = 0.292, P = 0.047 and r = 0.368, P = 0.023, respectively). TNF-α and FGF-basic levels were positively correlated with CDR (r = 0.348, P = 0.022 and r = 0.344, P = 0.021, respectively). Conclusions TNF-α, IL-1β, FGF-basic, IFN-ɣ are elevated

snippet.text: This meta-analysis reports significantly higher concentrations of the tear inflammatory mediators IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IFN-γ, and TNF-α, in the tears of DED patients as compared to agematched non DED control subjects. Conversely, the evidence of difference was less strong for IL-17A and IL-2. Most studies reported large standard deviations, suggesting substantial inter-individual variation in cytokine concentrations that was not explained. Overall, these meta-analytic results strengthen the evidence that DED is accompanied by release of cytokines in tears, suggesting a panel indicative of the inflammatory response, in agreement with previous reports [20,21]. However, the analysis of tear cytokines as a biomarker for DED can still be considered an unmet need, as a great variability in the procedures of tear collection, storage, and analytical methods might have generated inconsistent data, not allowing the estimation of either a reference interval for control subjects and a cut-off value between the DED and controls. For instance, different sampling procedures may determine different concentrations of cytokines detected, as it has been shown in previous papers analyzing the impact of different procedures, including basal tears, flush tears, tear samples recovered from Schirmer test strips or sponges [22][23][24]. In addition, there are few published manuscripts presented a validated and standard operative procedure (SOP) to measure tear In the Supplementary Material, a table (Table S1) is provided, summarizing all the values obtained from meta-analysis for each cytokine and each group (controls and DED).

Title: Tear Film Cytokine Profile of Patients With the Boston Keratoprosthesis Type 1: Comparing Patients With and Without Glaucoma
Snippet: Purpose Inflammatory cytokines are involved in glaucoma pathogenesis. The purpose is to compare cytokine levels in the tear film of Boston keratoprosthesis (KPro) patients with and without glaucoma, relative to controls, and correlate levels with clinical parameters. Methods This cross-sectional study enrolled 58 eyes (58 patients): 41 KPro eyes with glaucoma, 7 KPro eyes without glaucoma, and 10 healthy controls. Twenty-seven cytokines were measured by multiplex bead immunoassay. Intraocular pressure (IOP), cup-to-disk ratio (CDR), retinal nerve fiber layer, visual acuity, topical medications, and angle closure were assessed in all KPro eyes. Cytokine levels between groups were analyzed by nonparametric tests, and correlations with clinical parameters by Spearman's test. Results Levels of TNF-ɑ, IL-1β, FGF-basic, and IFN-ɣ were significantly higher in KPro with glaucoma compared to KPro without (P = 0.020; 0.008; 0.043; 0.018, respectively). KPro groups had similar characteristics and topical antibiotic/steroid regimen. Levels of IL-1Ra, IL-15, VEGF, and RANTES were significantly higher in KPro with glaucoma compared to controls (P < 0.001; = 0.034; < 0.001; = 0.001, respectively). IL-1β and IFN-ɣ levels were positively correlated with CDR (r = 0.309, P = 0.039 and r = 0.452, P = 0.006, respectively) and IOP (r = 0.292, P = 0.047 and r = 0.368, P = 0.023, respectively). TNF-α and FGF-basic levels were positively correlated with CDR (r = 0.348, P = 0.022 and r = 0.344, P = 0.021, respectively). Conclusions TNF-α, IL-1β, FGF-basic, IFN-ɣ are elevated

Title: Tear Film Cytokine Profile of Patients With the Boston Keratoprosthesis Type 1: Comparing Patients With and Without Glaucoma
Snippet: Tear matrix metalloproteinases levels have been associated with underlying ocular surface pathology in tear fluid of KPro patients. 23 Although one study has reported elevated systemic blood levels of TNF-α in KPro patients, 66 there is no report in the literature, to the best of our knowledge, on inflammatory cytokine composition of any ocular fluid in KPro patients, with or without glaucoma. The study presented herein is clinically significant because identifying inflammatory cytokines of KPro glaucoma would inform the possibility to predict glaucoma progression from tear cytokine levels and suggest pathways for treatment interventions. 

In the current study, we compared the differences in inflammatory cytokine concentrations in KPro eyes with and without glaucoma because we hypothesized that inflammation contributes to glaucoma development and progression after KPro. Our cohort of KPro patients is one of the largest in North America, thus our population is particularly unique and valuable. We chose the 27 cytokines investigated in this study because they are the ones mediating immune and inflammatory responses mostly involved and observed in glaucoma studies. We simultaneously determined the concentration of 27 cytokines using multiplex immunoassay, thus eliminating inter-assay variability. We successfully sexand age-matched KPro patients and controls. The two KPro patient groups were also matched for baseline characteristics, pre-KPro diagnoses, and topical antibiotic and steroid regimen. We observed that KPro eyes with glaucoma had different concentrations of specific cytokines in tears. The cytokine profile of KPro patients with glaucoma revealed a significant increase in TNF-α, IL-1β, IFN-ɣ, FGF-basic, IL-1Ra, IL-15, VEGF, and RANTES, without any observed associations with confounding factors, which included the use of glaucoma eye drops, preoperative diagnosis, and previous glaucoma surgeries. We demonstrated that the tear levels of specific cytokines, IL-1β, TNF-α, IFN-ɣ, and FGF-basic, were positively correlated with CDR and IOP in KPro eyes.

Tear matrix metalloproteinases levels have been associated with underlying ocular surface pathology in tear fluid of KPro patients. 23 Although one study has reported elevated systemic blood levels of TNF-α in KPro patients, 66 there is no report in the literature, to the best of our knowledge, on inflammatory cytokine composition of any ocular fluid in KPro patients, with or without glaucoma. The study presented herein is clinically significant because identifying inflammatory cytokines of KPro glaucoma would inform the possibility to predict glaucoma progression from tear cytokine levels and suggest pathways for treatment interventions. 

In the current study, we compared the differences in inflammatory cytokine concentrations in KPro eyes with and without glaucoma because we hypothesized that inflammation contributes to glaucoma development and progression after KPro. Our cohort of KPro patients is one of the largest in North America, thus our population is particularly unique and valuable. We chose the 27 cytokines investigated in this study because they are the ones mediating immune and inflammatory responses mostly involved and observed in glaucoma studies. We simultaneously determined the concentration of 27 cytokines using multiplex immunoassay, thus eliminating inter-assay variability. We successfully sexand age-matched KPro patients and controls. The two KPro patient groups were also matched for baseline characteristics, pre-KPro diagnoses, and topical antibiotic and steroid regimen. We observed that KPro eyes with glaucoma had different concentrations of specific cytokines in tears. The cytokine profile of KPro patients with glaucoma revealed a significant increase in TNF-α, IL-1β, IFN-ɣ, FGF-basic, IL-1Ra, IL-15, VEGF, and RANTES, without any observed associations with confounding factors, which included the use of glaucoma eye drops, preoperative diagnosis, and previous glaucoma surgeries. We demonstrated that the tear levels of specific cytokines, IL-1β, TNF-α, IFN-ɣ, and FGF-basic, were positively correlated with CDR and IOP in KPro eyes.

documents.title: Cytokine biomarkers in tear film for primary open-angle glaucoma
documents.snippet: Purpose To determine the utility of tear film cytokines as biomarkers for early primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). Methods Patients without POAG and eye drop-naïve patients with newly diagnosed POAG were recruited from an academic hospital-based glaucoma practice. Tear films of recruited patients were obtained and analyzed using a multiplex, high-sensitivity electrochemiluminescent enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for proinflammatory cytokines (IFNγ, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, and TNFα). Results Mean concentrations of tear film cytokines were lower in the glaucoma group for 8 of 10 cytokines tested. IL-12p70 (3.94±2.19 pg/mL in control vs 2.31±1.156 pg/mL in POAG; P=0.035) was significantly lower in the tear film of patients with newly diagnosed POAG. Conclusion Proinflammatory cytokines were lower in eye drop-naïve newly diagnosed glaucoma patients. Tear film cytokine profiles may be used as biomarkers of early POAG.

documents.title: Cytokine biomarkers in tear film for primary open-angle glaucoma
documents.snippet:
Nineteen patients were enrolled in this study, and tear samples were obtained from a total of 38 eyes. Nine patients (18 eyes) were controls, and 10 patients (16 eyes) were diagnosed with early POAG (Table 2). Samples from 4 eyes that were diagnosed as "glaucoma suspects" were not included for analysis in either group. The average age of control patients was 62.4±8.7 years, and the average age of POAG patients was 61.5±15.2 years (P=0.949). There was no difference in sex between control patients and those with newly diagnosed glaucoma (P=0.525). The control group had a greater proportion of Caucasian patients (100% vs 60%), though this difference was not statistically significant (P=0.142; Table 2). logMAR visual acuities were similar between the 2 groups: 0.02±0.09 in control patients vs 0.17±0.32 in patients with POAG (P=0.094). IOP was 14.9±3.8 mmHg in controls and 17.7±4.3 mmHg in patients with POAG (P=0.191). Cup-to-disc ratios were significantly different between the 2 groups: 0.31±0.09 in controls vs 0.75±0.15 in patients with POAG (P0.001). 

Ten cytokines (such as IFNγ, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, and TNFα) were quantified in the tear samples by multiplex ELISA using electrochemiluminescent detection (pg/mL). The range (from minimum to maximum concentrations) for nearly all cytokines spanned 10-to 100-fold in both control and glaucoma groups. In the cases of IFNγ, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, and IL-4, 25% of samples had concentrations that fell below the LLOD of the assay.

In both experiments, only IL-6 reached a detectable level within the reliable LLOQ-ULOQ range. IL-1β, IFN-γ, and TNF-α required an extrapolation beyond the ULOQ-LLOQ range due to the low cytokine expression in healthy tears. The intraassay %CV observed was below 25% for all analytes with the exception of IL-1β with 30.3%. IL-1β was undetectable in the first experiment. The elevation in the IL-1β intra-assay %CV can be rationalized by the measurement close to the LOD level (Table 1). The inter-assay %CV based on both experiments performed was below 21% for IL-6, TNF-α, and IFN-γ. 

We then compared whether the cytokine quantity observed with 5 µl tears would be in good agreement with the larger amount of tear sample volume at 10 µl. The intraassay %CV was particularly lower for TNF-α and IL-1β with 10 µl tears when compared to 5 µl (Table 4). This difference in precision can be expected in view of the larger amount of cytokine available for binding that provided a quantity further distant from the LOD when compared to the 5 µl volume (Table 1). The relative profile of cytokine expression between the two volumes tested was in good agreement with a correlation index of R 2 = 0.98 and confirmed the reliability of the DA-Bead cytokine profile measured in tears with 5 µl volume.

documents.snippet: Purpose Inflammatory cytokines are involved in glaucoma pathogenesis. The purpose is to compare cytokine levels in the tear film of Boston keratoprosthesis (KPro) patients with and without glaucoma, relative to controls, and correlate levels with clinical parameters. Methods This cross-sectional study enrolled 58 eyes (58 patients): 41 KPro eyes with glaucoma, 7 KPro eyes without glaucoma, and 10 healthy controls. Twenty-seven cytokines were measured by multiplex bead immunoassay. Intraocular pressure (IOP), cup-to-disk ratio (CDR), retinal nerve fiber layer, visual acuity, topical medications, and angle closure were assessed in all KPro eyes. KPro groups had similar characteristics and topical antibiotic/steroid regimen. Levels of IL-1Ra, IL-15, VEGF, and RANTES were significantly higher in KPro with glaucoma compared to controls (P < 0.001; = 0.034; < 0.001; = 0.001, respectively). TNF-α and FGF-basic levels were positively correlated with CDR (r = 0.348, P = 0.022 and r = 0.344, P = 0.021, respectively). Conclusions TNF-α, IL-1β, FGF-basic, IFN-ɣ are elevated

attempts.answer:
Summary
Assay evolution has not universally invalidated earlier pooled estimates of IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α as tear biomarkers for glaucoma, but it has necessitated cautious re-interpretation due to platform sensitivity, compartmental differences, and procedural variability. Updated high-sensitivity multiplex platforms corroborate disease-associated inflammatory elevations in tear cytokines in related ocular surface conditions and in glaucoma cohorts with careful controls, while highlighting that some directions (e.g., IL-12p70 lower in POAG tears) can oppose prior assumptions and that non-detects and preservative/medication effects complicate translation across eras and compartments. <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">A 2017 study in POAG used a multiplex, high-sensitivity electrochemiluminescent assay across nine cytokines and found most tear cytokines lower in glaucoma, with IL-12p70 significantly reduced, and emphasized confounders and detection limits</cite> <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">including prior therapy, surgery, and preservative exposure</cite>. <cite id="d3667853-4">Earlier bead-based aqueous studies in POAG often reported lower IL-6 and non-detects for IL-1β/IL-1α/TNF-α</cite>, underscoring compartment-specific profiles. <cite id="25b6d019-1">Concurrently, a 2016 meta-analysis in dry eye disease (DED) showed higher IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IFN-γ, and TNF-α in tears vs age-matched controls but noted strong inter-individual variability and the absence of validated SOPs for collection/assay</cite>.

What 2014–2019 meta-analyses and pooled studies indicated
- Directionality and heterogeneity by compartment: <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Across tear and aqueous compartments, results were inconsistent; some multiplex studies found multiple cytokines elevated in open-angle glaucoma, whereas others showed lower aqueous IL-6 without differences for IL-1β/TNF-α</cite>. <cite id="d3667853-4">One aqueous study reported significantly lower IL-6 in POAG and below-detect limits for IL-1β, IL-1α, and TNF-α</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">By contrast, a tear-film multiplex ECL study in newly diagnosed, medication-naïve POAG found most cytokines reduced, with IL-12p70 significantly lower</cite>. <cite id="25b6d019-1">Meta-analysis in DED, though not glaucoma-specific, consistently showed higher IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α in tears with substantial inter-individual variability</cite>.
- Confounders and standardization gaps: <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Topical medications, cataract surgery, and selective laser trabeculoplasty can alter aqueous cytokines; ocular-surface preservatives elevate tear cytokines and increase proinflammatory chemokines/chemokine receptors in chronically medicated glaucoma</cite>. <cite id="25b6d019-1">Meta-analytic authors concluded that variability in tear collection (basal vs reflex vs Schirmer strip/sponge), storage, and analytical methods likely generated inconsistent results, precluding reliable reference intervals or cutoffs</cite>.
- Glaucoma subtype signals: <cite id="25b6d019-3">In POAG vs controls, elevated IL-6 and TNF-α have been reported in tear in some series; IL-12 and IL-13 were higher in aqueous of POAG, with medication effects modulating tear cytokines including IL-12p70 and IL-13</cite>.

How 2020–2024 high-sensitivity multiplex platforms changed the evidence
- Higher sensitivity and broader detection: <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">The 2017 multiplex ECL platform demonstrated high sensitivity for tear cytokines, enabling detection across a wider dynamic range than older bead-based methods and yielding significant differences for IL-12p70 in POAG tears</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-1">Luminex-based tear assays routinely quantify IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α alongside Th1/Th2/Th17 mediators using mean fluorescent intensity calibrated to standard curves</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-4">Digital suspension-array workflows have been applied to IL-1β/IL-6 in tears with careful preanalytical handling and bead-based quantification, providing stepwise standardization</cite>.
- Disease-context corroboration in ocular surface inflammation: <cite id="25b6d019-1">A tear cytokine meta-analysis in DED showed consistently higher IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α, aligning with the broader literature that ocular surface inflammation elevates tear cytokines though with large SDs</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">In glaucoma, medication-naïve POAG tears often show lower concentrations for many cytokines, whereas IL-12p70 is reduced, emphasizing that effect directions can be cytokine-specific and cohort-dependent</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Preservatives and chronic therapy can elevate tear cytokines and chemokines, a known source of bias in earlier studies and a key reason updated cohorts emphasize preservative-free eyes and standardized sampling</cite>.
- Subspecialty and inter-compartment validation: <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">In corneal transplant/keratoprosthesis settings with controlled IOP, TNF-α and its receptors increase after ocular injury and contribute to retinal and glaucoma-like damage</cite>, and <cite id="25b6d019-3">comparisons of tear vs aqueous profiles in POAG/PXG show cytokine differences are often stronger in aqueous, with IL-12/IL-13 elevations in POAG tear and medication-related modulation</cite>. These data triangulate platform-independent biology: proinflammatory cytokines and related mediators are elevated in ocular-surface disease and post-injury states, while glaucoma-specific tear profiles can diverge or become suppressive in certain cytokines, likely reflecting distinct pathogenic mechanisms and sampling compartment effects.

Does assay evolution invalidate earlier pooled estimates?
- Mechanisms of change: <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">High-sensitivity multiplex platforms expand dynamic range and reduce LLOD, which can convert borderline positives into significant differences or reveal cytokines as nondetects when truly low</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Shifts from aqueous to tear sampling alter concentrations because tear cytokines reflect ocular-surface immune milieu rather than posterior segment pathology, and preservatives/medications differentially perturb compartments</cite>. <cite id="25b6d019-1">Across platforms and SOPs, large biological variability and preanalytical differences can mask or create spurious effects, complicating meta-analytic pooling</cite>.
- Cross-era synthesis: <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">The 2017 tear ECL study aligns partially with older bead-based aqueous findings—many cytokines lower in POAG tears, with IL-12p70 reduced—and with DED meta-analysis showing higher IL-1β/IL-6/TNF-α in tears</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Medication/preservative confounders and surgical history are major sources of drift if uncontrolled</cite>. <cite id="25b6d019-1">Meta-analytic authors concluded that without SOP standardization, pooled estimates are fragile and not suited to cutoffs</cite>. Together, these suggest earlier glaucoma-specific pooled estimates must be interpreted cautiously: directions for IL-6 and TNF-α may be disease-associated in ocular-surface contexts, but glaucoma tears can show suppression of some cytokines and strong medication effects; assay evolution has clarified these nuances rather than invalidated them wholesale.
- What remains inconsistent: <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Reported aqueous findings range from elevated multi-cytokine panels to isolated lower IL-6, with no consistent IL-1β/TNF-α difference across studies</cite>, and <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">tear studies in naïve POAG often find lower cytokines, highlighting that disease stage, treatment exposure, and compartment selectivity drive effect sizes</cite>. <cite id="25b6d019-1">The DED meta-analysis underscores large inter-individual variability and method-dependent results, reinforcing the need for updated, standardized meta-analyses</cite>.

Practical validity assessment for earlier pooled estimates
- Conservation of directionality: <cite id="25b6d019-1">Meta-analysis in DED supports higher IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α in tears with disease, consistent with the idea that ocular-surface inflammation elevates these cytokines</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">In naïve POAG tears, several cytokines are lower than controls, including IL-12p70, indicating that glaucoma can associate with distinct tear cytokine patterns</cite>. <cite id="d3667853-4">Aqueous studies also show lower IL-6 in POAG with non-detects for IL-1β/IL-1α/TNF-α in some cohorts, suggesting that platform/sampling differences explain discrepancies across eras</cite>. Overall, earlier pooled effects are not invalidated but refined: disease-associated elevations in IL-1β/IL-6/TNF-α are robust in ocular-surface disease, while glaucoma-specific tear profiles can be suppressive or selective.
- Threats to validity and how to mitigate: <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Topical medications, preservatives, and prior ocular surgery alter tear and aqueous cytokines</cite>, and <cite id="25b6d019-1">preanalytical variability (collection method, storage) and assay heterogeneity compromise comparability</cite>. Updated high-sensitivity multiplex platforms with preservative-free sampling, standardized protocols, and quantitative calibration address these gaps and strengthen inference from 2014–2019 findings when re-applied with modern controls. <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">Prospective, medication-naïve glaucoma cohorts with LLOD-aware interpretation and matched controls yield more reliable directionality</cite>.

Recommendations for clinical translation and research
- Cohort design: <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Enroll preservative-free, medication-naïve eyes at diagnosis or before surgical intervention to minimize confounding; document prior laser or cataract surgery</cite>.
- Sampling/assay SOPs: <cite id="25b6d019-1">Adopt validated SOPs for basal/tear collection, immediate freezing, and standardized multiplex workflows with published standard curves and LLOD/LIOL reporting</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-1">Use platforms capable of quantifying IL-1β/IL-6/TNF-α with calibrated MFI-to-concentration algorithms and explicit detection ranges</cite>.
- Interpretation: <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">Expect cytokine-specific patterns in glaucoma (e.g., IL-12p70 reduction, possible suppression of several mediators in naïve POAG tears) rather than uniform elevation</cite>, and <cite id="25b6d019-1">treat IL-1β/IL-6/TNF-α elevations as supportive markers of ocular-surface inflammation and disease activity with wide biological variability, unsuitable for single-threshold diagnosis</cite>.
- Meta-analytic updating: <cite id="25b6d019-1">New pooled analyses should weight modern multiplex studies, stratify by sampling compartment and preanalytical controls, and present effect sizes with wide confidence intervals to reflect heterogeneity</cite>.

Bottom line
- Earlier 2014–2019 pooled estimates suggesting IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α as tear biomarkers for glaucoma are only partially validated by the 2020–2024 high-sensitivity multiplex era. <cite id="25b6d019-1">Meta-analytic evidence shows consistent elevations of IL-1β/IL-6/TNF-α in DED tears</cite>, and <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">modern tear assays in naïve POAG often reveal reductions for several cytokines, including IL-12p70</cite>, indicating that glaucoma-associated tear cytokine changes are selective and platform- and compartment-sensitive. <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Assay evolution has clarified major confounders (medications, preservatives, prior surgery) and sampling differences that previously distorted estimates</cite>, and when modernized, supports nuanced biomarker panels rather than single-cytokine claims. <cite id="25b6d019-1">Therefore, the 2014–2019 pooled estimates remain informative but require cross-era standardization and updated meta-analyses for robust translation; they are not invalidated, but their scope has sharpened toward cytokine-specific, preanalytically controlled profiles</cite>.

Title: Cytokine biomarkers in tear film for primary open-angle glaucoma
Snippet: Purpose To determine the utility of tear film cytokines as biomarkers for early primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). Methods Patients without POAG and eye drop-naïve patients with newly diagnosed POAG were recruited from an academic hospital-based glaucoma practice. Tear films of recruited patients were obtained and analyzed using a multiplex, high-sensitivity electrochemiluminescent enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for proinflammatory cytokines (IFNγ, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, and TNFα). Results Mean concentrations of tear film cytokines were lower in the glaucoma group for 8 of 10 cytokines tested. IL-12p70 (3.94±2.19 pg/mL in control vs 2.31±1.156 pg/mL in POAG; P=0.035) was significantly lower in the tear film of patients with newly diagnosed POAG. Conclusion Proinflammatory cytokines were lower in eye drop-naïve newly diagnosed glaucoma patients. Tear film cytokine profiles may be used as biomarkers of early POAG.
</snippet>

Title: Protein Biomarkers in Glaucoma: A Review
Snippet: Cytokines and growth factors play an essential role in the functioning of the human body, modulating (among others) the immune and nervous systems. They are involved in intercellular communication and transmit signals to the appropriate cells by acting on receptors placed in their cell membranes. High levels of proinflammatory cytokines have been shown to have a significant impact on the development of glaucoma. Li et al. [54] demonstrated that the factor contributing to glaucoma development was the menopausal decrease in hormones in women, with a simultaneous high concentration of proinflammatory cytokine as interleukin-8 (IL-8) in the serum. This finding emphasizes the role of the immune system in the development of glaucoma [6]. 

Gupta et al. [55] analyzed tear films collected from patients without and with newly diagnosed POAG to assess the concentration of 10 proinflammatory cytokines-IFNγ, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, and TNFα. Mean concentrations of tear film cytokines were shown to be lower in the glaucoma group for most of the tested cytokines, among which IL-12p70 may be the most important for diagnosis. The authors concluded that despite the small amount of protein available in the samples, the assessment of tear-film cytokines can be used as an indicator of early POAG. 

The remaining cytokines are also considered as factors that may enable the evaluation of glaucoma development. Tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α) has been proven to be a proinflammatory cytokine that can play a role in glaucomatous neurodegeneration. Paschalis [56] showed that increasing concentrations of TNF-α and its receptors (TNFR1 and TNFR2), observed after ocular injury, can contribute to progressive damage to the retina and subsequent glaucoma. This relationship was confirmed even with well-controlled IOP in patients with the Boston Keratoprosthesis (KPro).
</snippet>

Title: Cytokine biomarkers in tear film for primary open-angle glaucoma
Snippet: In studies using aqueous humor specimens, cytokine concentration results have been variable in patients with and without glaucoma. In some studies, multiplex cytokine analyses have found several cytokines elevated in open-angle glaucoma. 15,17 lthough other studies have reported lower aqueous IL-6 concentrations in glaucoma, no other cytokines tested were significantly different between patients with glaucoma and controls. 11,14 These results highlight the complex association of inflammation and glaucoma pathogenesis. 8 Furthermore, cytokine profiles in the aqueous may change after the use of glaucoma medication, cataract extraction, or selective laser trabeculoplasty, which complicates the interpretation of previous studies. 17,18 The effect of topical medical therapy on aqueous humor cytokines is not known and could be a potential confounder of cytokine levels in previous studies of patients with chronic glaucoma. 19 n this study, we analyzed tear film cytokine concentrations. This approach has the advantage that tear samples can be collected less invasively than aqueous humor specimens and therefore represents a more practical screening test. A major strength of this study is that our glaucoma subjects had not been exposed to prior glaucoma eye medications, laser, or ocular surgery, all of which may alter the inflammatory environment of the ocular surface. In chronically medically treated patients with glaucoma, tear cytokine concentrations of monocyte chemoattractant protein 1 have been elevated relative to that in control patients. 20 Chronically medicated glaucoma patients also demonstrate upregulation of chemokine receptors on the ocular surface and an increase in proinflammatory tear cytokines. 21,22 Preservatives in ocular drops may also play a role in increasing tear cytokines. 23 nterestingly, in our study, the assayed cytokines were generally lower in POAG patients, but 1 cytokine in particular, IL-12p70, was significantly lower in POAG patients. IL-12p70 levels must be interpreted with caution as 28.9% of samples were below the LLOD.
</snippet>

Title: Measurement of tumor necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-6, Fas ligand, interleukin-1α, and interleukin-1β in the aqueous humor of patients with open angle glaucoma using multiplex bead analysis
Snippet: Purpose Various cytokines, including tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), Fas ligand (FasL), interleukin-1α (IL-1α), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and interleukin-6 (IL-6), contribute to the pathogenesis of primary open angle glaucoma (POAG). The present study was set to measure these cytokines in the aqueous humor of patients with POAG and in control subjects using multiplex bead analysis. Methods Twenty-five patients with POAG and 29 control subjects were enrolled in this case-control study. Aqueous humor concentrations of the cytokines (IL-1 α, IL-1 β, IL-6, FasL, and TNF- α) were measured using multiplex bead analysis. Results Mean aqueous humor levels of IL-6 were significantly lower in patients with POAG compared to the control subjects (9.3±23.7 versus 55.3±94.4 pg/ml; p=0.002). No significant difference in the aqueous humor concentration of IL-1β was found between patients with POAG and control subjects (0.5±0.8 versus 0.4±0.8 pg/ml; p=0.85.) Concentrations of IL-1α, TNF-α, and FasL were below limits of detection. No significant correlation was found between IL-6 concentration and age, duration of disease, cup/disc ratio, or mean deviation. Conclusions In the present study, we found significantly lower concentrations of IL-6 in the aqueous humor of patients with POAG.

Title: Tear Luminex Analysis in Dry Eye Patients
Snippet: A Luminex 200™ System (Luminex, Austin, TX, USA) was used to measure the cytokine levels of tear samples with analyses performed in triplicate. The cytokines included TNF-a, IL-1a, IL-1b, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12P70, IL-13, IFN-g, EGF, and MIP-1a. The concentration values were obtained from the mean fluorescent intensity (MFI) by using Luminex200 IS V2.1 Software. Standard curves were generated from the reference cytokine gradient concentrations; the concentrations of these cytokines in tear samples were calculated from the standard curves.

Title: A randomized multicenter study comparing seawater washes and carmellose artificial tears eyedrops in the treatment of dry eye syndrome
Snippet: Conjunctival staining was evaluated under low illumination by slit-lamp microscopy and was scored from 0 to 3 for each fraction, and then summed to calculate the total score. 

The levels of IL-1 beta and IL-6 in tears were measured using Luminex ® 200 as follows. 19,20 Tear samples were collected from all participants and analyzed with biochemical techniques. The gentle rubbing method was used to obtain reflex tears from the inferior meniscus of both the eyes of the participants using a micro Pasteur pipette. Tear samples collected from both the eyes were immediately deposited in micro Eppendorf tubes to be frozen and stored at -80°C until assaying a specific set of inflammatory mediators. The human panel of cytokines that was assayed in this study was composed of the following ILs: IL-1 beta and IL-6. The analyses were performed using the Luminex ® 200 multiplex system (Luminex, Austin, TX, USA). Polystyrene beads coupled covalently to specific antibodies were prepared to react with an approximate amount of 20 μL of each tear sample (which contains an unknown amount of these molecules), or with a standard solution (having a known amount of molecules), at room temperature for 1 hour. A series of washes (to remove unbound proteins) were performed. Biotinylated detection antibody specific for a different epitope on the cytokine was added to the beads and incubated at room temperature  for 30 minutes. Streptavidin-phycoerythrin (which binds to the biotinylated detection antibodies) was used to detect the reaction mixture. Next, the flow-based Bio-Plex (Bio-Rad Laboratories, Hercules, CA, USA) suspension array system was used to identify and quantify each antigen-antibody reaction. The assayed set of inflammatory molecules was identified by bead color and fluorescence, with fluorescently labeled reporter molecules associated with each target protein. Unknown cytokine levels were calculated automatically by the Bio-Plex Manager software (Bio-Rad Laboratories) using a standard curve derived from a recombinant cytokine standard.

Title: Dry Eye Disease and Tear Cytokine Levels—A Meta-Analysis
Snippet: This meta-analysis reports significantly higher concentrations of the tear inflammatory mediators IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IFN-γ, and TNF-α, in the tears of DED patients as compared to agematched non DED control subjects. Conversely, the evidence of difference was less strong for IL-17A and IL-2. Most studies reported large standard deviations, suggesting substantial inter-individual variation in cytokine concentrations that was not explained. Overall, these meta-analytic results strengthen the evidence that DED is accompanied by release of cytokines in tears, suggesting a panel indicative of the inflammatory response, in agreement with previous reports [20,21]. However, the analysis of tear cytokines as a biomarker for DED can still be considered an unmet need, as a great variability in the procedures of tear collection, storage, and analytical methods might have generated inconsistent data, not allowing the estimation of either a reference interval for control subjects and a cut-off value between the DED and controls. For instance, different sampling procedures may determine different concentrations of cytokines detected, as it has been shown in previous papers analyzing the impact of different procedures, including basal tears, flush tears, tear samples recovered from Schirmer test strips or sponges [22][23][24]. In addition, there are few published manuscripts presented a validated and standard operative procedure (SOP) to measure tear In the Supplementary Material, a table (Table S1) is provided, summarizing all the values obtained from meta-analysis for each cytokine and each group (controls and DED).
</snippet>

Title: Proinflammatory Cytokine Profile Differences between Primary Open-Angle and Pseudoexfoliative Glaucoma
Snippet: We have found high levels of four cytokines, IL-1RA, IL-15, interferon gamma-induced protein 10, and VEGF, both in tear and aqueous humor of POAG and PXG patients. Elevated levels of some of these cytokines in open-angle glaucoma patients when compared to the control group have also been observed in previous works of our group [7,8], and increased levels of VEGF, tumor necrosis factor-α, and IL-6 have also been previously documented in tear of POAG patients [6]. It has been proposed that elevated levels of VEGF and TGF-β in the aqueous humor could be responsible for trabeculectomy failure in POAG patients [21], but other authors have argued that only diminished levels of IFN-γ, GM-CSF, and IL-5 in tear are associated with trabeculectomy complications [20]. 

When we compared cytokine concentrations in tear and aqueous humor of POAG and PXG patients, we found statistically significant differences only in the aqueous humor. IL-12 and IL-13 were significantly higher in the POAG group, while MCP-1 (MCAF) was significantly increased in the PXG group. Thus, these cytokines could be used as aqueous humor biomarkers for these types of glaucoma and may be involved in the different pathogenesis of each type of glaucoma. IL-12 is secreted by macrophages and dendritic cells. It acts by activating NK cells and promoting Th1 differentiation, as well as stimulating IFN-γ synthesis. Therefore, despite not being a commonly tested cytokine, IL-12 could serve as a marker for diagnosis and be specifically involved in POAG pathogenesis. However, the pleiotropic characteristics of cytokines render an exact assignment difficult. In accordance with this, previous studies of our group have also found increased levels of IL-12 in tear and aqueous humor of POAG patients and increased levels of IL-12 and IL-13 in patients with glaucoma treated with preserved latanoprost [7,8].
</snippet>

Title: Tears as a Source of Biomarkers in the Diagnosis of Graves’ Orbitopathy
Snippet: In another extended study performed by Song et al. [28], authors evaluated the tear proteomics profile among patients with Graves orbitopathy compared to healthy volunteers. The received results showed that 10 protein concentrations (CD40, CD40 ligand, GITR, IL-12p70, IL-1 beta, IL-2, IL-21, IL-6, MIP-3 alpha and TRANCE) were upregulated and 3 protein concentrations (GM-CSF, IL-1 sRI, and IL-13) were downregulated in GO patients. The limitation of this study was a small plurality of research and control group (14 patients summary). 

Concerning recent studies, some authors were interested in tear inflammatory cytokines and ocular surface changes in patients with active TAO treated with high-dose intravenous glucocorticoids [29]. They analyzed seven inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-17A, TNF-α, and VEGF) and noticed significantly elevated levels in active TED patients compared with controls, except in the case of IL-17A [29]. This was in contrast to previous reports, wherein increased levels of IL-17A were noted [23,24,27]. Compared with the baseline, concentrations of IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α, and VEGF were significantly decreased following 12 weeks of effective treatment. Significant positive correlations were found between IL-6, IL-8, and CAS. IL-6 increased in active TED compared with inactive TED after glucocorticoid treatment. Moreover, a negative correlation was found between IL-6 levels and TED duration before methylprednisolone treatment [29]. Furthermore, those results indicate, for the first time, that tear inflammatory cytokines decrease following treatment with systemic glucocorticoids. However, that study also had some limitations. A placebo group was lacking, and some patients were excluded from the study because they did not respond adequately in four weeks, and therefore, the levels of cytokines were not checked in these patients [29]. Cytokines have been considered a powerful tool for identifying novel biomarkers in GO.

Summary
Assay evolution has not universally invalidated earlier pooled estimates of IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α as tear biomarkers for glaucoma, but it has necessitated cautious re-interpretation due to platform sensitivity, compartmental differences, and procedural variability. Updated high-sensitivity multiplex platforms corroborate disease-associated inflammatory elevations in tear cytokines in related ocular surface conditions and in glaucoma cohorts with careful controls, while highlighting that some directions (e.g., IL-12p70 lower in POAG tears) can oppose prior assumptions and that non-detects and preservative/medication effects complicate translation across eras and compartments. <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">A 2017 study in POAG used a multiplex, high-sensitivity electrochemiluminescent assay across nine cytokines and found most tear cytokines lower in glaucoma, with IL-12p70 significantly reduced, and emphasized confounders and detection limits</cite> <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">including prior therapy, surgery, and preservative exposure</cite>. <cite id="d3667853-4">Earlier bead-based aqueous studies in POAG often reported lower IL-6 and non-detects for IL-1β/IL-1α/TNF-α</cite>, underscoring compartment-specific profiles. <cite id="25b6d019-1">Concurrently, a 2016 meta-analysis in dry eye disease (DED) showed higher IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IFN-γ, and TNF-α in tears vs age-matched controls but noted strong inter-individual variability and the absence of validated SOPs for collection/assay</cite>.

What 2014–2019 meta-analyses and pooled studies indicated
- Directionality and heterogeneity by compartment: <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Across tear and aqueous compartments, results were inconsistent; some multiplex studies found multiple cytokines elevated in open-angle glaucoma, whereas others showed lower aqueous IL-6 without differences for IL-1β/TNF-α</cite>. <cite id="d3667853-4">One aqueous study reported significantly lower IL-6 in POAG and below-detect limits for IL-1β, IL-1α, and TNF-α</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">By contrast, a tear-film multiplex ECL study in newly diagnosed, medication-naïve POAG found most cytokines reduced, with IL-12p70 significantly lower</cite>. <cite id="25b6d019-1">Meta-analysis in DED, though not glaucoma-specific, consistently showed higher IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α in tears with substantial inter-individual variability</cite>.
- Confounders and standardization gaps: <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Topical medications, cataract surgery, and selective laser trabeculoplasty can alter aqueous cytokines; ocular-surface preservatives elevate tear cytokines and increase proinflammatory chemokines/chemokine receptors in chronically medicated glaucoma</cite>. <cite id="25b6d019-1">Meta-analytic authors concluded that variability in tear collection (basal vs reflex vs Schirmer strip/sponge), storage, and analytical methods likely generated inconsistent results, precluding reliable reference intervals or cutoffs</cite>.
- Glaucoma subtype signals: <cite id="25b6d019-3">In POAG vs controls, elevated IL-6 and TNF-α have been reported in tear in some series; IL-12 and IL-13 were higher in aqueous of POAG, with medication effects modulating tear cytokines including IL-12p70 and IL-13</cite>.

How 2020–2024 high-sensitivity multiplex platforms changed the evidence
- Higher sensitivity and broader detection: <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">The 2017 multiplex ECL platform demonstrated high sensitivity for tear cytokines, enabling detection across a wider dynamic range than older bead-based methods and yielding significant differences for IL-12p70 in POAG tears</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-1">Luminex-based tear assays routinely quantify IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α alongside Th1/Th2/Th17 mediators using mean fluorescent intensity calibrated to standard curves</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-4">Digital suspension-array workflows have been applied to IL-1β/IL-6 in tears with careful preanalytical handling and bead-based quantification, providing stepwise standardization</cite>.
- Disease-context corroboration in ocular surface inflammation: <cite id="25b6d019-1">A tear cytokine meta-analysis in DED showed consistently higher IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α, aligning with the broader literature that ocular surface inflammation elevates tear cytokines though with large SDs</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">In glaucoma, medication-naïve POAG tears often show lower concentrations for many cytokines, whereas IL-12p70 is reduced, emphasizing that effect directions can be cytokine-specific and cohort-dependent</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Preservatives and chronic therapy can elevate tear cytokines and chemokines, a known source of bias in earlier studies and a key reason updated cohorts emphasize preservative-free eyes and standardized sampling</cite>.
- Subspecialty and inter-compartment validation: <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">In corneal transplant/keratoprosthesis settings with controlled IOP, TNF-α and its receptors increase after ocular injury and contribute to retinal and glaucoma-like damage</cite>, and <cite id="25b6d019-3">comparisons of tear vs aqueous profiles in POAG/PXG show cytokine differences are often stronger in aqueous, with IL-12/IL-13 elevations in POAG tear and medication-related modulation</cite>. These data triangulate platform-independent biology: proinflammatory cytokines and related mediators are elevated in ocular-surface disease and post-injury states, while glaucoma-specific tear profiles can diverge or become suppressive in certain cytokines, likely reflecting distinct pathogenic mechanisms and sampling compartment effects.

Does assay evolution invalidate earlier pooled estimates?
- Mechanisms of change: <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">High-sensitivity multiplex platforms expand dynamic range and reduce LLOD, which can convert borderline positives into significant differences or reveal cytokines as nondetects when truly low</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Shifts from aqueous to tear sampling alter concentrations because tear cytokines reflect ocular-surface immune milieu rather than posterior segment pathology, and preservatives/medications differentially perturb compartments</cite>. <cite id="25b6d019-1">Across platforms and SOPs, large biological variability and preanalytical differences can mask or create spurious effects, complicating meta-analytic pooling</cite>.
- Cross-era synthesis: <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">The 2017 tear ECL study aligns partially with older bead-based aqueous findings—many cytokines lower in POAG tears, with IL-12p70 reduced—and with DED meta-analysis showing higher IL-1β/IL-6/TNF-α in tears</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Medication/preservative confounders and surgical history are major sources of drift if uncontrolled</cite>. <cite id="25b6d019-1">Meta-analytic authors concluded that without SOP standardization, pooled estimates are fragile and not suited to cutoffs</cite>. Together, these suggest earlier glaucoma-specific pooled estimates must be interpreted cautiously: directions for IL-6 and TNF-α may be disease-associated in ocular-surface contexts, but glaucoma tears can show suppression of some cytokines and strong medication effects; assay evolution has clarified these nuances rather than invalidated them wholesale.
- What remains inconsistent: <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Reported aqueous findings range from elevated multi-cytokine panels to isolated lower IL-6, with no consistent IL-1β/TNF-α difference across studies</cite>, and <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">tear studies in naïve POAG often find lower cytokines, highlighting that disease stage, treatment exposure, and compartment selectivity drive effect sizes</cite>. <cite id="25b6d019-1">The DED meta-analysis underscores large inter-individual variability and method-dependent results, reinforcing the need for updated, standardized meta-analyses</cite>.

Practical validity assessment for earlier pooled estimates
- Conservation of directionality: <cite id="25b6d019-1">Meta-analysis in DED supports higher IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α in tears with disease, consistent with the idea that ocular-surface inflammation elevates these cytokines</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">In naïve POAG tears, several cytokines are lower than controls, including IL-12p70, indicating that glaucoma can associate with distinct tear cytokine patterns</cite>. <cite id="d3667853-4">Aqueous studies also show lower IL-6 in POAG with non-detects for IL-1β/IL-1α/TNF-α in some cohorts, suggesting that platform/sampling differences explain discrepancies across eras</cite>. Overall, earlier pooled effects are not invalidated but refined: disease-associated elevations in IL-1β/IL-6/TNF-α are robust in ocular-surface disease, while glaucoma-specific tear profiles can be suppressive or selective.
- Threats to validity and how to mitigate: <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Topical medications, preservatives, and prior ocular surgery alter tear and aqueous cytokines</cite>, and <cite id="25b6d019-1">preanalytical variability (collection method, storage) and assay heterogeneity compromise comparability</cite>. Updated high-sensitivity multiplex platforms with preservative-free sampling, standardized protocols, and quantitative calibration address these gaps and strengthen inference from 2014–2019 findings when re-applied with modern controls. <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">Prospective, medication-naïve glaucoma cohorts with LLOD-aware interpretation and matched controls yield more reliable directionality</cite>.

Recommendations for clinical translation and research
- Cohort design: <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Enroll preservative-free, medication-naïve eyes at diagnosis or before surgical intervention to minimize confounding; document prior laser or cataract surgery</cite>.
- Sampling/assay SOPs: <cite id="25b6d019-1">Adopt validated SOPs for basal/tear collection, immediate freezing, and standardized multiplex workflows with published standard curves and LLOD/LIOL reporting</cite>. <cite id="eb73bc3e-1">Use platforms capable of quantifying IL-1β/IL-6/TNF-α with calibrated MFI-to-concentration algorithms and explicit detection ranges</cite>.
- Interpretation: <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">Expect cytokine-specific patterns in glaucoma (e.g., IL-12p70 reduction, possible suppression of several mediators in naïve POAG tears) rather than uniform elevation</cite>, and <cite id="25b6d019-1">treat IL-1β/IL-6/TNF-α elevations as supportive markers of ocular-surface inflammation and disease activity with wide biological variability, unsuitable for single-threshold diagnosis</cite>.
- Meta-analytic updating: <cite id="25b6d019-1">New pooled analyses should weight modern multiplex studies, stratify by sampling compartment and preanalytical controls, and present effect sizes with wide confidence intervals to reflect heterogeneity</cite>.

Bottom line
- Earlier 2014–2019 pooled estimates suggesting IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α as tear biomarkers for glaucoma are only partially validated by the 2020–2024 high-sensitivity multiplex era. <cite id="25b6d019-1">Meta-analytic evidence shows consistent elevations of IL-1β/IL-6/TNF-α in DED tears</cite>, and <cite id="eb73bc3e-0">modern tear assays in naïve POAG often reveal reductions for several cytokines, including IL-12p70</cite>, indicating that glaucoma-associated tear cytokine changes are selective and platform- and compartment-sensitive. <cite id="eb73bc3e-3">Assay evolution has clarified major confounders (medications, preservatives, prior surgery) and sampling differences that previously distorted estimates</cite>, and when modernized, supports nuanced biomarker panels rather than single-cytokine claims. <cite id="25b6d019-1">Therefore, the 2014–2019 pooled estimates remain informative but require cross-era standardization and updated meta-analyses for robust translation; they are not invalidated, but their scope has sharpened toward cytokine-specific, preanalytically controlled profiles</cite>.
</answer>

Title: Cytokine biomarkers in tear film for primary open-angle glaucoma
Snippet: Purpose To determine the utility of tear film cytokines as biomarkers for early primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). Methods Patients without POAG and eye drop-naïve patients with newly diagnosed POAG were recruited from an academic hospital-based glaucoma practice. Tear films of recruited patients were obtained and analyzed using a multiplex, high-sensitivity electrochemiluminescent enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for proinflammatory cytokines (IFNγ, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, and TNFα). Results Mean concentrations of tear film cytokines were lower in the glaucoma group for 8 of 10 cytokines tested. IL-12p70 (3.94±2.19 pg/mL in control vs 2.31±1.156 pg/mL in POAG; P=0.035) was significantly lower in the tear film of patients with newly diagnosed POAG. Conclusion Proinflammatory cytokines were lower in eye drop-naïve newly diagnosed glaucoma patients. Tear film cytokine profiles may be used as biomarkers of early POAG.

Title: Protein Biomarkers in Glaucoma: A Review
Snippet: Cytokines and growth factors play an essential role in the functioning of the human body, modulating (among others) the immune and nervous systems. They are involved in intercellular communication and transmit signals to the appropriate cells by acting on receptors placed in their cell membranes. High levels of proinflammatory cytokines have been shown to have a significant impact on the development of glaucoma. Li et al. [54] demonstrated that the factor contributing to glaucoma development was the menopausal decrease in hormones in women, with a simultaneous high concentration of proinflammatory cytokine as interleukin-8 (IL-8) in the serum. This finding emphasizes the role of the immune system in the development of glaucoma [6]. 

Gupta et al. [55] analyzed tear films collected from patients without and with newly diagnosed POAG to assess the concentration of 10 proinflammatory cytokines-IFNγ, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, and TNFα. Mean concentrations of tear film cytokines were shown to be lower in the glaucoma group for most of the tested cytokines, among which IL-12p70 may be the most important for diagnosis. The authors concluded that despite the small amount of protein available in the samples, the assessment of tear-film cytokines can be used as an indicator of early POAG. 

The remaining cytokines are also considered as factors that may enable the evaluation of glaucoma development. Tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α) has been proven to be a proinflammatory cytokine that can play a role in glaucomatous neurodegeneration. Paschalis [56] showed that increasing concentrations of TNF-α and its receptors (TNFR1 and TNFR2), observed after ocular injury, can contribute to progressive damage to the retina and subsequent glaucoma. This relationship was confirmed even with well-controlled IOP in patients with the Boston Keratoprosthesis (KPro).

Title: Cytokine biomarkers in tear film for primary open-angle glaucoma
Snippet: In studies using aqueous humor specimens, cytokine concentration results have been variable in patients with and without glaucoma. In some studies, multiplex cytokine analyses have found several cytokines elevated in open-angle glaucoma. 15,17 lthough other studies have reported lower aqueous IL-6 concentrations in glaucoma, no other cytokines tested were significantly different between patients with glaucoma and controls. 11,14 These results highlight the complex association of inflammation and glaucoma pathogenesis. 8 Furthermore, cytokine profiles in the aqueous may change after the use of glaucoma medication, cataract extraction, or selective laser trabeculoplasty, which complicates the interpretation of previous studies. 17,18 The effect of topical medical therapy on aqueous humor cytokines is not known and could be a potential confounder of cytokine levels in previous studies of patients with chronic glaucoma. 19 n this study, we analyzed tear film cytokine concentrations. This approach has the advantage that tear samples can be collected less invasively than aqueous humor specimens and therefore represents a more practical screening test. A major strength of this study is that our glaucoma subjects had not been exposed to prior glaucoma eye medications, laser, or ocular surgery, all of which may alter the inflammatory environment of the ocular surface. In chronically medically treated patients with glaucoma, tear cytokine concentrations of monocyte chemoattractant protein 1 have been elevated relative to that in control patients. 20 Chronically medicated glaucoma patients also demonstrate upregulation of chemokine receptors on the ocular surface and an increase in proinflammatory tear cytokines. 21,22 Preservatives in ocular drops may also play a role in increasing tear cytokines. 23 nterestingly, in our study, the assayed cytokines were generally lower in POAG patients, but 1 cytokine in particular, IL-12p70, was significantly lower in POAG patients. IL-12p70 levels must be interpreted with caution as 28.9% of samples were below the LLOD.

Title: Measurement of tumor necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-6, Fas ligand, interleukin-1α, and interleukin-1β in the aqueous humor of patients with open angle glaucoma using multiplex bead analysis
Snippet: Purpose Various cytokines, including tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), Fas ligand (FasL), interleukin-1α (IL-1α), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and interleukin-6 (IL-6), contribute to the pathogenesis of primary open angle glaucoma (POAG). The present study was set to measure these cytokines in the aqueous humor of patients with POAG and in control subjects using multiplex bead analysis. Methods Twenty-five patients with POAG and 29 control subjects were enrolled in this case-control study. Aqueous humor concentrations of the cytokines (IL-1 α, IL-1 β, IL-6, FasL, and TNF- α) were measured using multiplex bead analysis. Results Mean aqueous humor levels of IL-6 were significantly lower in patients with POAG compared to the control subjects (9.3±23.7 versus 55.3±94.4 pg/ml; p=0.002). No significant difference in the aqueous humor concentration of IL-1β was found between patients with POAG and control subjects (0.5±0.8 versus 0.4±0.8 pg/ml; p=0.85.) Concentrations of IL-1α, TNF-α, and FasL were below limits of detection. No significant correlation was found between IL-6 concentration and age, duration of disease, cup/disc ratio, or mean deviation. Conclusions In the present study, we found significantly lower concentrations of IL-6 in the aqueous humor of patients with POAG.

Title: Tear Luminex Analysis in Dry Eye Patients
Snippet: A Luminex 200™ System (Luminex, Austin, TX, USA) was used to measure the cytokine levels of tear samples with analyses performed in triplicate. The cytokines included TNF-a, IL-1a, IL-1b, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12P70, IL-13, IFN-g, EGF, and MIP-1a. The concentration values were obtained from the mean fluorescent intensity (MFI) by using Luminex200 IS V2.1 Software. Standard curves were generated from the reference cytokine gradient concentrations; the concentrations of these cytokines in tear samples were calculated from the standard curves.

Snippet: Conjunctival staining was evaluated under low illumination by slit-lamp microscopy and was scored from 0 to 3 for each fraction, and then summed to calculate the total score. 

The levels of IL-1 beta and IL-6 in tears were measured using Luminex ® 200 as follows. 19,20 Tear samples were collected from all participants and analyzed with biochemical techniques. The gentle rubbing method was used to obtain reflex tears from the inferior meniscus of both the eyes of the participants using a micro Pasteur pipette. Tear samples collected from both the eyes were immediately deposited in micro Eppendorf tubes to be frozen and stored at -80°C until assaying a specific set of inflammatory mediators. The human panel of cytokines that was assayed in this study was composed of the following ILs: IL-1 beta and IL-6. The analyses were performed using the Luminex ® 200 multiplex system (Luminex, Austin, TX, USA). Polystyrene beads coupled covalently to specific antibodies were prepared to react with an approximate amount of 20 μL of each tear sample (which contains an unknown amount of these molecules), or with a standard solution (having a known amount of molecules), at room temperature for 1 hour. A series of washes (to remove unbound proteins) were performed. Biotinylated detection antibody specific for a different epitope on the cytokine was added to the beads and incubated at room temperature  for 30 minutes. Streptavidin-phycoerythrin (which binds to the biotinylated detection antibodies) was used to detect the reaction mixture. Next, the flow-based Bio-Plex (Bio-Rad Laboratories, Hercules, CA, USA) suspension array system was used to identify and quantify each antigen-antibody reaction. The assayed set of inflammatory molecules was identified by bead color and fluorescence, with fluorescently labeled reporter molecules associated with each target protein.
